lab.title: Your Hubble investigation
lab.intro: Acquire each supported galaxy, measure their line shifts yourself, then compare velocity with magnitude-based distance. This guide follows your saved data. It does not supply an expected redshift, align lines, grade accuracy or enter Hubble values.
lab.counts: Archived galaxy spectra: {archived}/{total} · Measured targets: {measured}/{total} · Complete Hubble targets: {rows}/{total}

lab.next.dataset: This workspace includes examples or other inputs. This guide tracks only the supported acquired galaxies. Save your work before clearing Hubble rows to build that separate dataset; the measurement log is retained.
lab.next.recipe: Next: open Hubble, add your saved galaxy measurements and select VIREO targets + student manual · M = −21.4 · fit through zero.
lab.next.inputs: Next: keep one Hubble row per acquired target and complete its apparent V, magnitude source and explicit target identification. Read each row’s status before interpreting the result.
lab.next.interpret: Your eight-target dataset is ready to interpret. Review your fitted relation, discuss the assumptions and limitations, then save and restore your investigation. This version supports eight of the 13 original Hubble.HTL galaxies. This is not a grade or a claim of original-runtime equivalence.
lab.duplicate: Repeated Hubble rows for the same acquired galaxy are not independent targets. Remove the extra Hubble row; keep the original measurement in the log.
lab.acquireHelp: Open Galaxy exposure. In Acquisition galaxy choose 36747 · UM-I – 1, 36773 · UM-I – 2, 54876 · CorBor – 2, or on the 0.4m telescope only 54875 · CorBor – 1, 54891 · CorBor – 3, NGC 7499 · Peg – 1, NGC 7501 · Peg – 2 and NGC 7503 · Peg – 3. Activate supported galaxy field, then Start galaxy exposure. Activation sets the exact supported pointing. Alternatively, choose the supported acquisition entry in the observatory, open the dome, point and switch to telescope view.
lab.acquisitionTime: Let useful counts accumulate before Analyze acquired galaxy; a positive exposure can still be too noisy to align. A 2–3 minute exposure is a practical starting point for inspection, not an accuracy guarantee. Pause exposure preserves counts; Cancel and discard clears that segment. Opening this guide alone does not pause exposure. Navigation away pauses/deactivates the live segment.
lab.measureHelp: Analyze acquired galaxy pauses and archives a snapshot. In the analyser choose the galaxy line list, set z step per tick and Apply step. Move the reference markers until the same shift aligns several absorption features. Use Full view if you need a wider interval. You decide whether the spectrum supports a measurement. Record measurement opens a confirmation; Cancel leaves the log unchanged, Save measurement records your result.
lab.stepHelp: The step controls comparison resolution, not an answer. You can begin with a comparison step such as 0.001 per tick, then choose a smaller step to refine. This is an example control resolution, not a measured redshift. Changing the step or Fine/Coarse preserves the current z; New adjustment returns to zero and requires a step again. No catalogue redshift is revealed. Return to Galaxy exposure for the next target, or reopen an archived spectrum to repeat a measurement.
lab.hubbleHelp: Open Hubble diagram & distances and Add saved measurements. For the acquired path choose VIREO targets + student manual · M = −21.4 · fit through zero. Enter an apparent V and its source for each row, then explicitly identify its acquired target. The reference cards below provide original workbook V values; copy them yourself if you choose that source. These are catalog references, not photometry from your spectrum.
lab.recipeHelp: Velocity comes from your saved manual z using v = c z. Distance follows the selected absolute-magnitude assumption. The VIREO/manual route fits through (0,0); the distinct workbook M = −21.0 route computes mean(v/D) and has no fitted line. Keep those interpretations separate. All rows must be complete; the fit requires at least two rows, and this guide follows all currently supported distinct acquired targets.
lab.saveHelp: Use Save session in Keep your work, or Save Hubble session. JSON includes the archived raw journals, controls, linked measurement log and Hubble drafts. Reload and Restore session to check that the same dataset returns. Export CSV and Export Hubble CSV provide readable tables and sources. CSV is not a replay backup. Save before closing the page or starting over.
lab.sspHelp: Download acquired SSP provides a 600-bin normalized spectrum plus telescope header. Reimporting it shows file claims and requires a new manual alignment; it cannot restore raw counts, timing, RNG or acquired provenance. Keep JSON for that. Inspect acquisition for measurement and Restore this acquisition in the telescope recover a stopped snapshot; activate explicitly to resume.
lab.interpretHelp: Use your plotted points and exported sources to explain what you measured and what you assumed. No expected slope or automatic mark is provided.
lab.reflect.data: Which quantities came from your line alignment, which from a documented V reference, and which were calculated under an assumed absolute magnitude?
lab.reflect.fit: What does the slope mean in the units shown? Why does forcing the intercept to zero impose a model? How does that differ from averaging v/D?
lab.reflect.errors: How might noisy spectra, manual alignment, luminosity differences and peculiar velocities affect the relation? Which effects did this bounded simulation actually include?
lab.reflect.environment: UM-I – 1 and UM-I – 2 share a grouping. CorBor – 1/2/3 share the verified CorBor field, and NGC 7499/7501/7503 share the NGC 7501 field. Do all your confirmed points sample independent environments? Explain why this bounded adapted exercise is not a new determination of H0.
lab.targets: Targets, progress and original V references
lab.referencesHelp: These values are supplied original reference data, not measured answers. No z or velocity from the workbook is used here. You may use another documented magnitude source; report it explicitly.
lab.recover.start: Choose an available Acquisition galaxy entry and activate its verified view. Revisit/reactivate after changing routes or targets. Analyse requires positive committed counts. Other catalogue pointings are not supported acquisitions.
lab.problem.noisy: The features are hard to align
lab.recover.noisy: Do not treat a short/noisy curve as a precise result. Inspect acquisition for measurement or reopen its snapshot, restore it in the telescope, activate and collect more counts. A new snapshot starts unconfigured comparison controls. A new seed resets the live segment; save first. Equal seeds reuse the same random stream and do not ensure independent realizations.
lab.recover.rows: Choose a recipe and read the status of every row. Supply a finite dot-decimal apparent V, its source and, for VIREO, its target identification. Editing V clears the source; enter the new source again. Empty, invalid or duplicate rows block the aggregate; none is silently discarded. Remove an accidental Hubble row without deleting its measurement.
lab.problem.repeat: Repeating a measurement changes the target count
lab.recover.repeat: Several spectra/measurements of one galaxy are still one target. Keep the preferred measurement for that target in Hubble. Label changes, SSP imports and original workbook examples cannot become an acquired target by name.

class.title: Classify a stellar spectrum
class.intro: Compare original practices, imported SP/SSP files or a replay-verified acquired star with the original main-sequence and luminosity atlases. Propose an MK spectral type and explain your own evidence; source identity does not supply an answer.
class.instructions: How to classify and keep your work
class.guide.choose: Choose Original practice library in Classification source and one of the 25 original practice objects, or choose an archived star acquisition. The current spectrum appears between adjacent main-sequence standards. Your library draft and each acquired snapshot have separate retained workspaces. You may also import SP/SSP for comparison here or open an imported analyser spectrum; each file retains separate manual work.
class.guide.compare: Choose Spectral atlas, then Standard pair or Previous/Next standard to compare original adjacent entries. Begin with the main sequence, then choose a luminosity atlas near your own temperature-class estimate. Original labels and order are preserved, including mixed nearby subtypes. The default displayed interval is 3900–4500 Å; Set classification wavelength range can widen it. No atlas or standard is selected as your answer.
class.guide.difference: For library practice select Standard − practice to inspect the signed difference in the bottom panel. Positive means the top standard has greater relative intensity. Practice grids match exactly; acquired grids differ, so acquired difference is disabled. There is no interpolation, best-match score or grade.
class.guide.answer: Select a row in the line table if useful. Write your proposed spectral type and describe features supporting it, including uncertainty. Review classification opens a confirmation; Cancel preserves your draft without adding a record. Save classification stores your own interpretation. Repeat for another practice object.
class.guide.save: Save complete investigation keeps raw acquisition journals, analyser measurements, Hubble work, practice progress and all acquired classification drafts/responses together. Reload and restore that JSON to continue. Practice-only version 1 files are still supported. CSV is a readable record export, not a backup.
class.limit: All 25 original practices and all eight ATLAS2.LST atlases are available: 13 main-sequence entries plus 25 luminosity entries in seven near-type groups. The supported acquired star can be compared from all three telescope profiles; eligible imported/acquired unknowns also support numerical readouts and photos under explicit grid guards. There is no automatic type, luminosity, temperature, distance or grade. Broader native imports, combined display, full cursor/zoom/pan tools and native result formats remain pending. Manual equivalent width can be measured anywhere in each spectrum's own coverage within 3500–7400 Å; the default view stays 3900–4500 Å.
class.source: Based on VIREO Manual pp. 24–27, CLASSHLP.TXT (Main Sequence before luminosity), the 24 November 2008 student manual pp. 3 and 7–10, ATLAS2.LST, its eight ATL files, CLASSIFY.LST and SPECLNS.LNL. Associations, labels and order come directly from original data. Number difference, display and session/CSV behavior are web adaptations; original runtime/x87 equivalence is unverified. Local research only.

classLab.title: Classify a practice star
classLab.intro: Compare one of the 25 original practice spectra with the original atlas standards, inspect its lines and decide its spectral type yourself. Nothing is graded and no answer is given; the steps only show what you have done.
classLab.adaptation: This guide, its checklist and the line table are web presentation; the native help screens and dialogs are not reproduced.
classLab.scopeOther: This guide follows the original practice library. Choose Original practice library in Classification source to see your progress. Acquired and imported spectra keep their own work.

classLab.step.choose.title: 1 · Choose a practice
classLab.step.choose.help: In Classification source keep Original practice library, then pick one of the 25 objects in Practice object. Wait until the original spectra are verified.
classLab.step.compare.title: 2 · Compare with the atlas
classLab.step.compare.help: Start with the main sequence atlas. Move through the standard pairs with Previous/Next until the practice lies between two neighbours, then try a luminosity atlas near that type. Standard − practice shows the signed difference.
classLab.step.inspect.title: 3 · Inspect lines and widths
classLab.step.inspect.help: Look at the lines that change with type. You may also measure an equivalent width. Either action completes this step.
classLab.step.inspect.table: Line table: pick a row to draw its marker on every pane. Rows outside the displayed window are labelled; Zoom in centres on the marker.
classLab.step.inspect.width: Equivalent width (optional): mark or type a center and two shoulders anywhere in the spectrum's allowed interval shown in the tool, then review and save it. Widen the view with Set classification wavelength range to see lines beyond 4500 Å.
classLab.step.inspect.reverse: Reverse trace displays (optional): turns the sampled traces upside down for viewing only. Turn it off to use the cursor or marks.
classLab.step.record.title: 4 · Record your classification
classLab.step.record.help: Write your proposed type and the features that support it, including any doubt. Review classification opens a check; Cancel or Escape keeps your draft, Save classification adds the record.
classLab.step.save.title: Save and restore
classLab.step.save.help: Save complete investigation downloads a file. After a reload, Restore complete investigation brings back your records, line choice and width records; recompute a width to see the same value.

classAtlas.mainHelp: Begin here to compare temperature-class patterns. To explore luminosity, choose the relevant original near-type atlas yourself. Changing atlas resets only its standard pair; your proposed answer and reasoning are retained.
classAtlas.luminosityHelp: These are the original luminosity-atlas labels and order. Some rows have slightly different spectral subtypes; they are not coerced to a single temperature. Compare patterns at a suitable type and justify your own MK classification, including uncertainty. Normalized curve height does not measure absolute luminosity or distance.
classAtlas.guide: The VIREO help recommends comparing the main sequence before selecting a luminosity atlas. The student manual introduces MK Roman numerals: I for supergiants, III for giants and V for main-sequence stars. Other numerals remain as supplied in the original atlas. No luminosity, radius, temperature or distance is calculated from this choice.
feature.title: Manual equivalent width
feature.intro: Measure an original practice spectrum by marking its center and two shoulders. You choose the continuum intensity at each shoulder; the tool does not choose it for you.
feature.manual: Use left < center < right inside the allowed interval shown above, with continuum intensities greater than 0 and at most 1. Dashed lines show your continuum and center. These decimal controls replace the original mouse selection.
feature.invalid: No measurement was saved. Check all five decimal inputs, the ordered region inside this spectrum's allowed interval, positive continuum levels up to 1, and the verified selected source/grid. Existing drafts and records were kept.

feature.region: Center {center} Å; shoulders {left} Å at {leftI} and {right} Å at {rightI}.
feature.converged: The declared Number adaptation met the recovered strict relative convergence test. This is not a physical error estimate or a native-runtime equivalence claim. Passing this stopping test does not bound the integration error.
feature.nonconverged: The strict relative convergence test did not pass within 20 refinements. This includes an exactly zero residual, whose relative threshold is also zero. The value is provisional and cannot be recorded. No absolute tolerance is substituted.
feature.portable: Manual region drafts are kept separately for each practice. Up to 20 width records travel with the classification/full investigation JSON. Only inputs and source identities are saved; select the same practice and recompute a record using its verified source. A cancelled calculation adds no record.
feature.limit: The recovered path uses a straight shoulder continuum, original endpoint-grid quadratic sampling, and refined trapezoids with extrapolation. Number arithmetic, decimal inputs and finite positive-continuum guards are web adaptations. This is not the same-grid difference plot. No automatic type, grade, Hubble point or physical luminosity is derived.

Eight original hotlist positions with unvalidated association or mixed variable fields, arbitrary pointing, R/I and native observation files remain unsupported. Restored optical observing tools require activation; Restore starts the Radio telescope paused with its receivers closed.

optical.title: Optical telescope
optical.defaults: These are the three original VIREO 1.504 compiled fallback profiles. User preference files are not loaded.
optical.choose: Telescope profile to inspect or select
optical.pending: Inspecting {name}. Apply to change the current telescope, or cancel to keep it.
optical.nominal: Names retain the original nominal labels. The stored millimetre values below are preserved, including differences from those labels.
optical.field.utOffset: UT minus local standard time · hours
optical.hubbleAccess: Access policy: original unrestricted Hubble mode. All three profiles can be selected here; no observing-time request or lottery is performed.
optical.storedAvailability: Stored request-mode availability: {chance}. This probability is inactive under the current unrestricted access policy.
optical.always: The default telescope is always available; no allocation request applies.
optical.requestMetadata: In restricted request mode only: a successful grant would allow {min}–{max} completed uses; rejected requests wait {wait} minutes before reapplying. This request workflow is not enabled here.
optical.siteLimit: Compiled site values feed the UT/sidereal and geometric horizon readouts. Horizon enforcement, physical site/time-dependent acquisition and daylight-saving corrections remain unavailable.
optical.evidenceHelp: Compiled constructor 0x5a3174, native Site Information 0x53e9e4 and Hubble access 0x58a8ca are bound to the preserved executable hash. Single values and Extended coordinate bytes are retained; displayed numbers are web projections, without a native execution oracle.
optical.switchHelp: Applying a different telescope stops and retains current segments, closes the preview dome and retains catalog pointing. Apply/Cancel and this retention policy are web adaptations. The verified star and three galaxies retain independent journals for all three telescopes.
optical.applied: Selected {name}. Observing segments were stopped and retained; the preview dome is closed.
optical.acquisitionLimit: This instrument has no admitted acquisition calibration for the selected telescope. Existing journals and manual measurements remain unchanged. All three compiled telescopes support verified star/three-galaxy spectroscopy, sky and the bounded photometry exercise with telescope-specific target domains.
starExposure.telescopeContext: Acquisition profile: {name}. Stored zero point {zero}; maximum committed interval {limit} ms. Telescope journals are independent.
starExposure.calibration: This segment: slit level {level}, stored zero point {zero}, source amplitude {source}, sky amplitude {sky}, elapsed multiplier50. These are native magnitude-calibration inputs; existing counts are never rescaled.
galaxyExposure.telescopeContext: Acquisition profile: {name}. Stored zero point {zero}; maximum committed interval1000ms. Each telescope/target retains a separate journal.
skyExposure.precisionGap: Paused: this interval reached an unresolved Number/x87 sampling boundary. No counts were added. Keep the stopped segment or explicitly prepare a new seeded exposure.
siteClock.title: Site clock · fixed UT scenario
siteClock.scope: Inspect the recovered VIREO sidereal calculation at the selected telescope's site in use: the compiled site, or your Site Parameters override (clocks and horizon only). This worksheet remains fixed until you apply another UT; its initial J2000 example is not the current observing time.
siteClock.format: Enter YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss, years 1900–2099, whole seconds in UT. The browser timezone is ignored.
siteClock.error: Enter a valid Gregorian date and UT from 1900 through 2099. Leap seconds are outside this worksheet. The applied scenario is unchanged.
siteClock.sidereal: Local mean sidereal time · decimal hours
siteClock.limits: Original polynomial and the longitude of the site in use (compiled or overridden); Number arithmetic and Gregorian input are declared browser adapters. Applied UT also feeds the shared clock and current-pointing geometric horizon readout, which the optional Limit Slewing can enforce. It does not synthesize site/time-dependent photons. Investigation backups preserve the applied UT and unapplied draft; site overrides and options are saved too.
runningClock.title: Observatory clock & spectral tracking
runningClock.scope: This control is shared by the visible sky and the verified spectral acquisitions. Tracking holds RA/Dec; tracking off drifts the pointing with the recovered VIREO 24-hour-per-clock-day branch and releases integration. Start/Pause control the shared observing clock.
runningClock.untracked: Tracking off · RA drifts while clock runs
runningClock.limit: Clock paused at a preview boundary: an interval exceeded 1000 ms, the 24-hour/date limit was reached, or declination lies outside ±85°. No uncommitted interval was added. Apply a supported UT or repoint, then start explicitly.
runningClock.limits: Pause or tracking changes release spectral integration first. The clock continues on supported spectral pages; leaving those pages, hiding the tab, saving/restoring or changing site/pointing/UT stops it. UT is a bounded observing scenario, not a recovered native spectral-file timestamp. Counts retain their own elapsed/RNG journals. Bounded motor commands now use this clock. With Limit Slewing on, a tracked target that sets below the horizon turns tracking off. Native global timer ordering, time-dependent photon synthesis and the separate photometer bench remain outside this connection.
instrumentAccess.currentHelp: Uses the current selected object and pointing without moving it. Tracking, narrow field and this exact verified target/profile must already match.
instrumentAccess.fieldUnavailable: Current pointing or tracking is outside this calibrated field. Its raster is hidden and no new photons are integrated; retained counts remain available for analysis/export.
instrumentAccess.released: Integration released because the shared observing clock or tracked field is no longer available. Committed counts and random state were kept.
instrumentAccess.ready: Spectral control ready · tracked, narrow and verified pointing.
instrumentAccess.tracking: Spectral control blocked · turn tracking on, then verify the current pointing or explicitly prepare the fixed field.
instrumentAccess.moving: Spectral control blocked · telescope movement has not completed.
instrumentAccess.finder: Spectral control blocked · switch to telescope view.
instrumentAccess.dome: Spectral control blocked · open the dome.
instrumentAccess.configuration: Spectral control blocked · this target/profile is not verified.
instrumentAccess.pointing: Spectral control blocked · the current selected object/pointing does not match this verified field.
instrumentAccess.photoSeparate: This exercise bench retains its own verified fields and integration model. The Observatory’s selected object and imported spectra do not select a photometer target; use the exercise list below. Entering this tool pauses the separate observatory clock/drive. Its notebook and counts are preserved.
instrumentAccess.photoOrchestration: Web orchestration: Activate points the actual telescope at this bench’s verified field (a pointed PLEIADES.HTL star or the current target), and Start requires that exact pointing with the dome open in telescope view. This pointing check is a browser guard, not a recovered native photometer rule.
horizon.label: Current pointing · geometric horizon
horizon.scope: Derived from the applied UT, the selected telescope's site in use (compiled, or your Site Parameters override) and the actual current RA/Dec, using the recovered optional horizon calculation. This is a geometric readout; no refraction, precession, extinction or local obstruction model is added.
horizon.angle: Hour angle · local sidereal time minus RA
horizon.above: Current pointing is above the configured geometric horizon.
horizon.at-or-below: Current pointing is at or below the configured geometric horizon.
horizon.precision-boundary: Near the strict horizon boundary: Number arithmetic cannot establish the original Extended comparison.
horizon.zenith: Near zenith or nadir: the displayed angle has limited Number precision.
horizon.enforcement: Limit Slewing: off (compiled default). This readout does not block pointing, tracking or acquisition. Turn Limit Slewing on under Optical Simulation Options to enforce this horizon.
instrumentAccess.protection: Web scope protection: changing tracking stops and deactivates this bounded spectral acquisition before an unverified offset can be used. This is not a claim about native photon behavior during drift. The native spectrometer disables its tracking button; its timer consumes prepared channel means.
drift.title: Read-only stellar drift detector
drift.scope: The actual current pointing is projected into the verified fixed stellar cache. This reconstruction follows the native cache-hit crop, nearest-object query and slit calculation for the three supported telescope profiles. It is separate from acquired counts and does not claim native cache history or motor timing.
drift.frameLabel: Read-only cached stellar detector at current pointing
drift.frameCaption: Reconstructed pre-overlay cache crop. The gold 3 × 19 slit overlay is not included in the sampled pixels.
drift.ready: Cached-field inspection available. Acquisition remains outside its fixed-field gate.
drift.unsupported-declination: Inspection unavailable: this cached trajectory admits only the original fixed declination. No new field is fabricated.
drift.cache-boundary: Inspection unavailable: this pointing needs an unadmitted cache reload/repaint. No pixels or throughput are extrapolated.
drift.precision-required: Inspection paused at an unresolved Number boundary of cache rounding or stellar slit admission. No original Extended decision is guessed.
drift.meanLimit: Readout only: no exposure means are refreshed and no photons or RNG draws are generated. The count chart and acquisition slit level above retain the stored fixed configuration. Native focus/reinitialization and retained/discarded buffer behavior remain pending.
skyProfiles.context: Acquisition profile: {name}. Recovered sky zero point {zero}; this profile has its own retained journal and seed.
skyProfiles.calibration: Sky magnitude19; recovered telescope zero point {zero}; Number sky mean {mean} per unit, elapsed multiplier50. No source contribution or sky subtraction is generated.
exposureIO.saved: Saved. Repeated saves preserve the same counts and random state.
exposureIO.loading: Reading exposure session. Current counts and random state are kept until validation completes.
exposureIO.kept: Session was not restored. Existing counts and random state were kept.
exposureIO.cancelled: Pending exposure restore cancelled. Existing counts and random state were kept.
exposureIO.empty: Investigation restored an empty exposure workspace. Activate a supported field to prepare an exposure.
ph.seriesProfile: {telescope} · filter {filter} · {seconds} s × {repeats} integrations · verified field and seeing.
ph.seriesHelp: Choose an original duration and 1–5 repeats before starting. Original compiled defaults are 1 s × 3; existing sessions keep their 0.1 s × 1 setting. Changing settings clears the current result, while confirmed notebook entries and normalized sky remain.
ph.seriesUnfinished: This unfinished series is not a completed reading and cannot enter the notebook. Stop retains committed counts and random state; Start resets series counters and continues that state.
ph.seriesCompleted: Integration series completed. Source plus sky counts and random state were retained. Enter your own target reading before starting another series.
ph.seriesStopped: Series stopped without creating a completed reading. Committed callback counts and random state were retained. Start resets counters and keeps the current seed.
ph.seriesGap: Series stopped: the callback gap exceeded {limit} ms or the clock was unavailable. No uncommitted callback was added. Committed counts and random state were retained.
ph.seriesLimit: The photometer session reached its callback, event or file-size limit. Save existing work before starting a new seeded session.
ph.seriesError: This series could not be completed within its supported count or numerical limits. Existing work and the last committed random state were kept.
ph.seriesPrecision: This callback requires unsupported numerical precision. The series stopped without committing it. Save existing work before choosing a new seeded session or supported settings.
ph.noteLimit: This note would exceed the session limit. Shorten it and confirm again, or cancel. Previous readings and notebook entries remain saveable.
ph.sampleCoverage: {available} of {total} original hotlist positions are observable in this telescope profile. The remaining {excluded} are outside its validated domain; missing contracts are not approximated.
ph.access.ready: Telescope ready · dome open, telescope view, pointing equals this photometer field.
ph.access.pointing: Start blocked · the telescope pointing does not equal this photometer field. Activate to point it explicitly.
ph.access.dome: Start blocked · the dome is closed.
ph.access.finder: Start blocked · switch the observatory to telescope view.
ph.access.moving: Start blocked · the telescope is moving.
ph.pointedRow: The telescope points exactly at PLEIADES.HTL entry {number} ({label}). Activate selects this star at its target position without moving the telescope.
ph.pointedUnavailable: The telescope points at PLEIADES.HTL entry {number} ({label}), which is unavailable here: {reason}. Activation is blocked; point at an admitted entry.
ph.pointedOutsideTelescope: The telescope points at PLEIADES.HTL entry {number} ({label}), which is outside the checked domain of {telescope}. Activation is blocked; choose an admitted telescope or another entry.
ph.pointedNone: The telescope is not on a PLEIADES.HTL star. Activate moves it explicitly to this bench’s field for {target}.
ph.pointedBlocked: Activation blocked: PLEIADES.HTL entry {number} ({label}) is not available for the selected telescope. No photometer event was recorded.
ph.activatedPointed: Pleiades photometer activated on PLEIADES.HTL entry {number} ({label}) at its target position. Take fresh sky through each filter before reading the star.
ph.pointingReleased: Telescope context released because the telescope is no longer on this photometer field. No new photons were drawn; counts and notebook remain.
pa.title: Exercise color–magnitude analysis
pa.intro: Use your confirmed B/V notebook pairs to reproduce the printed 2008 paper-and-overlay distance exercise. Enter a vertical shift yourself; compare the central main sequence by eye.
pa.coverage: Explicitly paired targets: {count}. Points outside the original plot axes: {hidden}; all values remain in the table. The eight unavailable hotlist positions stay excluded.
pa.chartTitle: Manual exercise V versus B−V diagram
pa.chartDescription: B−V increases from −0.4 to 1.8 left to right. Apparent V increases from 0 at the top to 25 at the bottom. Green points are manual notebook values, labelled by original hotlist number. An entered modulus shifts the orange standard sequence vertically.
pa.legend: Green circles: your manual pairs and original hotlist numbers. Orange squares: 14 printed calibration stars; dashed segments are visual guides. No curve is shown until you enter a shift.
pa.fitHelp: Move the standard sequence vertically by entering m−M. Keep B−V fixed. Seek a visual fit to the central pattern; the manual warns that cool red stars are scattered. At least two confirmed pairs are needed to save a fit. No optimizer or catalog answer is used.
pa.invalid: Enter a finite modulus from −25 to 40 in steps of 0.1 magnitude. These are web input limits.
pa.preview: Unconfirmed preview: {pc} pc · {ly} ly · {percent} versus the manual’s historical 410 ly reference. Full investigation saves preserve this draft separately; only a confirmed fit enters the photometer journal.
pa.historical: Signed difference from the manual’s historical 410 ly reference
pa.resultHelp: Saved with {count} explicit B/V pair references. D=10×10^((m−M)/5) pc; 1 pc=3.26 ly as in the manual. Changing a selected B/V pair invalidates this confirmation. A changed preview does not replace it until confirmed.
pa.unconfirmed: No distance fit is confirmed. Full investigation saves preserve the unapplied shift, including blank or invalid text. The photometer-only JSON contains confirmed fits and observing history.
pa.standardHelp: Source: Photoelectric Photometry of the Pleiades, 11-24-2008, p11, caption Table 2 (the prose calls it Table 3), adapted from Allen, Astrophysical Quantities. Spectral labels and the unusual −0.7 at B−V=0 are retained as printed.
pa.limits: This is the paper-manual workflow using the admitted VIREO observing sample; edition equality is unverified. The 410 ly comparison is a historical exercise reference. No age, isochrone, reddening/extinction correction, membership classification, automatic fit or uncertainty estimate is supplied. Number/Math precision is not original x87 equivalence.
pa.chartHelp: On narrow screens, scroll the diagram horizontally or inspect the full values in the table. Coincident points share a label; they remain separate table rows.
pa.confirmError: The cluster fit was not confirmed. Check the manual B/V pairs and enter a shift from −25 to 40 in steps of 0.1 magnitude.
nc.title: Native ZAMS and isochrone trials
nc.intro: Compare your manual B/V pairs with the recovered VIREO ZAMS and original discrete isochrones. Choose a trial reddening, apparent modulus, age and metallicity yourself; no optimizer or catalog answer is used.
nc.manual: Explicit manual pairs: {count}. These are the same confirmed notebook pairs listed in the manual analysis above.
nc.axes: The diagram uses the fixed paper-manual axes above. Scroll horizontally on narrow screens. Native HR autoscaling and cluster reddening presets are not ported.
nc.chartTitle: Manual observations with trial native ZAMS and isochrone
nc.chartDescription: Green circles are manual V/B−V notebook pairs. Gold is the native five-knot ZAMS. Purple is one original isochrone at the explicitly selected age and metallicity. Curves move by the pupil’s entered apparent modulus and color excess.
nc.legend: Green: manual observations. Gold: native ZAMS. Purple: original isochrone. Models are theoretical reference curves, not acquired observations.
nc.nodes: ZAMS nodes: {zams}. Isochrone rows: {iso}. Nodes outside the fixed axes: {hidden}; all remain in the values table.
nc.correctExtinction: Apply the original optional extinction correction to distance
nc.correctionHelp: The native correction uses A_V=3×E(B−V), not 3.1. It changes distance only: neither curve receives an additional vertical shift. When unchecked, distance uses the apparent modulus alone. This is an explicit pupil choice; no cluster default is supplied.
nc.interpretation: Your interpretation of the trial fit (optional)
nc.incomplete: Complete valid trial fields to add an isochrone and enable confirmation. No confirmed result changes while you edit.
nc.loadError: The selected model could not load. Retry the selected model; confirmed work is retained.
nc.preview: Unconfirmed trial: {age} Myr · {distance} pc · applied A_V={av} mag. This is a chosen model age, not an automatically measured age.
nc.fitSource: Confirmed against {count} explicit manual B/V pairs. Recalculating any selected color invalidates both confirmations.
nc.unconfirmed: No native model fit is confirmed. Full investigations preserve unapplied trial text separately; the photometer JSON records only explicit confirmations.
nc.curveHelp: All original isochrone rows remain in file order. There is no sorting, age interpolation, metallicity interpolation, smoothing or decimation. Values include only your explicit plotting shifts.
nc.limits: Six original metallicities and 50 discrete ages are available (about 63 Myr to 17.8 Gyr). The hidden seventh “019nov” file is excluded. The eight unvalidated observing positions remain excluded. No automatic membership, turnoff classification, fitted age, uncertainty estimate or original runtime/x87 equivalence is claimed.
nc.error: The model fit was not confirmed. Check two explicit manual B/V pairs and the bounded trial settings; stop any active integration first.
db.title: Star-cluster database laboratory
db.intro: Load an original reference dataset, compare the native ZAMS and isochrones by eye, and confirm your own interpretation. Reference catalog values are separate from acquired observations and your photometer notebook.
db.loading: Loading the verified cluster reference dataset…
db.cancelled: Dataset load cancelled. Existing measurements and interpretation are retained.
db.loadError: The reference dataset could not load or verify. Retry the load; existing work is retained.
db.boundary: All 16 original reference fields are available. These are catalog datasets; observing availability, including the eight unavailable entries in PLEIADES.HTL, is unchanged. Native autoscaling and uncertainty estimates remain unavailable.
db.loaded: {cluster} reference dataset loaded: {count} catalog points with B−V. No photons or notebook readings were created.
db.presetHelp: When Load selected dataset first loads a dataset successfully, its new notebook starts with this catalog reddening copied into its unapplied trial. A notebook first created by Retry dataset load does not get this copy: its modulus, E(B−V), age and metallicity start blank, so press this button to copy the catalog value. This button copies it again at any time. You can change it; editing it makes it your manual input. A stored zero is preserved without inferring a physical meaning. Distance modulus, age, metallicity and interpretation remain your choices.
db.presetCopied: Catalog reddening copied into the trial. Confirm your chosen model separately.
db.catalogDraft: Unapplied reddening source: original {cluster} catalog preset.
db.manualDraft: Unapplied reddening source: your manual input.
db.catalogConfirmed: Confirmed reddening source: original {cluster} catalog preset.
db.manualConfirmed: The reddening remains a manual choice unless you explicitly copy the catalog preset.
db.manualStart: Choose the modulus, reddening, trial age and metallicity yourself. Extra isochrone offset starts at {offset}.
db.curveIntro: Compare the loaded reference dataset with native VIREO theoretical curves. Choose every trial and confirm your own interpretation. No automatic fit, age, membership decision or catalog distance answer is supplied.
db.referencePoints: Reference catalog points: {count}. These are dataset values, not your acquired photometer measurements.
db.legend: Green: reference catalog data. Gold: native ZAMS. Purple: original isochrone. Your photometer notebook is unchanged.
db.fitSource: Confirmed against {count} loaded reference catalog points. Your acquired/manual B/V measurements are separate.
db.axes: The plot uses the fixed native HR axes (V 2–18, B−V −0.5 to +2.5). On narrow screens, scroll it horizontally. All reference values remain in the reference table, including any outside these axes. Native autoscaling is not implemented.
db.chartTitle: Reference cluster data with manual native model trials
db.chartDescription: Green circles are the loaded {cluster} reference catalog points, not photometer readings. Gold is the native ZAMS and purple is the chosen original isochrone. Every model adjustment is a manual trial.
db.limits: The original finite model and control ranges may not give a satisfactory fit for every dataset. Record your own conclusion. No automatic fit, membership, uncertainty estimate or original runtime/x87 equivalence is claimed. The historical grid extends to about17.8Gyr.
db.pendingHelp: The chooser is an unapplied selection. The active dataset and its confirmed result remain until you explicitly load the selection.
db.notebookHelp: Each dataset has an independent manual notebook. When Load selected dataset first loads a dataset successfully, it copies only its catalog E(B−V) into an editable, unapplied trial; modulus, age, metallicity and interpretation start blank. A notebook first created by Retry dataset load (for example after a failed first load) gets no catalog E(B−V): its modulus, E(B−V), age and metallicity start blank, and Use catalog E(B−V) copies the catalog value when you choose. Returning to an earlier dataset restores its own confirmation and unapplied text exactly, including a discarded or blank trial. No fit or interpretation is copied between datasets.
db.comparisonHelp: Only explicitly confirmed trials appear here. Ages, distances and metallicities are your model choices, not catalog answers or automatically determined cluster properties. Choose a dataset above and load it to continue its own notebook.
ce.title: Manual reference-point exclusions
ce.help: Choose a catalog record and confirm its exclusion from your diagram. This is your own selection, not a membership decision supplied by the software. Original reference values and all acquired measurements remain intact.
ce.choose: Reference point to inspect or exclude
ce.guard: Changing exclusions retains your trial text and requires a new explicit model confirmation for that dataset. At least two included points are required to confirm.
ce.changed: Reference selection changed. Your trial text was retained; confirm a new interpretation when ready.
ce.used: Included reference points: {included} of {total}. Exclusions are your own choices; acquired photometry is separate.
ce.confirmHelp: Exclude {id} from this dataset’s diagram? Its original values remain available in the reference table. You can restore all excluded points.
ce.inspectedMarker: Orange outline: your inspected point, when included and within the fixed axes. This is a selection cue, not a membership classification.
db.prefilled: New {cluster} notebook: the catalog E(B−V) = {ebv} was copied into your unapplied trial. It is editable; changing it makes the reddening your manual input. Nothing is confirmed.
db.hrDrawn: Drawn inside the fixed native axes: {inside}. Outside these axes (not drawn; listed in the values table): {outside}.
db.frameNote: Recovered native HR frame (0x542480): 28 px per magnitude and 120 px per B−V magnitude. Browser SVG and Number arithmetic stand in for the original GDI/x87 pixels; native autoscaling and the paint-box extent are not recovered. Marker size is a web choice.
db.sliderHelp: Each slider follows the text above it and moves in the original steps (0.01; age 0.05). Moving a slider writes only its own field and never confirms a result. db.reportNoIsochrone: The isochrone section appears only when the whole trial is valid and the selected original model has loaded.
db.reportNote: This follows the recovered parameter report (0x543d90) for exactly what the diagram shows. The distance line appears only when the optional extinction correction is checked, as in the original; the apparent-modulus preview distance is not printed. Rounding uses browser Number arithmetic, not the original Extended arithmetic.
db.printNote: Browser printing is a web adaptation; the original print path (0x542fc8) is not recovered.
db.printError: The browser could not start printing. The report above is unchanged.
clusterLab.open: Student guide: cluster ages and distances
clusterLab.title: Ages and distances of star clusters
clusterLab.intro: Compare a reference cluster with theoretical ZAMS and isochrone curves, choose your own fit by eye, and record your interpretation. Check marks show actions you have taken; they never grade your fit.
clusterLab.counts: {done} of {total} database steps show an action or result.
clusterLab.noDataset: No reference dataset is loaded yet.
clusterLab.next.load: Next: choose a reference dataset and press Load selected dataset.
clusterLab.next.inspect: Next: open the reference data values or choose a point to inspect.
clusterLab.next.trial: Next: enter or slide a complete trial and choose a metallicity model.
clusterLab.next.confirm: Next: when you are satisfied, write your interpretation and confirm your chosen model fit.
clusterLab.next.report: Next: open View/Print Parameters to read your report.
clusterLab.next.preserve: All database steps show an action. Keep your work with Save investigation (see below).
clusterLab.progressHelp: Each mark is recomputed from what the laboratory currently shows for the active dataset. Changing exclusions or the trial can remove a mark again. Saving is not tracked here.
clusterLab.step.load.title: Load a reference cluster
clusterLab.step.load.help: Choose one of the 16 original reference datasets and press Load selected dataset. A notebook created by that first successful load starts with the catalog E(B−V) copied in; you may change it. A notebook created by Retry dataset load instead does not copy E(B−V); press Use catalog E(B−V) to copy it.
clusterLab.step.inspect.title: Inspect the data
clusterLab.step.inspect.help: Open Inspect all reference data values, or choose a point to inspect. Points outside the fixed axes are listed in the table but not drawn. You may exclude points you judge unsuitable; that is your own choice.
clusterLab.step.trial.title: Fit the ZAMS and an isochrone by eye
clusterLab.step.trial.help: Shift the ZAMS with the apparent modulus and E(B−V) until it follows the lower main sequence. Then choose a metallicity and log age so the isochrone follows the turnoff. Type values or use the sliders.
clusterLab.step.confirm.title: Confirm your chosen fit
clusterLab.step.confirm.help: Write your interpretation and press Confirm chosen model fit. Editing afterwards keeps the confirmed result until you confirm again.
clusterLab.step.report.title: Read the parameter report
clusterLab.step.report.help: Open View/Print Parameters. It lists the modulus, reddening, metallicity, log age and age in million years. Check the optional extinction correction to include the estimated distance in parsecs.
clusterLab.preserve.heading: Keep your work
clusterLab.preserve.save: Press Save investigation to download a file with your notebooks, exclusions and confirmed results.
clusterLab.preserve.restore: Later, use Restore investigation JSON with that file to continue. The guide does not track whether a file was saved.
clusterLab.own.heading: Your own observations (Pleiades)
