ownHr.reportEmpty: No valid ZAMS is shown, so the report lists only the source. Enter a valid modulus and E(B−V).
ownHr.limits: This web view stands in for the original Record-to-file step. No automatic fit, membership decision, uncertainty estimate, original DAT record or original runtime/x87 equivalence is claimed. The photometer’s model-fit section shows the same confirmation; its paper-manual distance fit is separate.
ph.openHr: Plot my pairs in HR Data from Observations
ph.openHrHelp: Opens the cluster database page with your confirmed B/V pairs on the native HR axes. The photometer is stopped and deactivated first, with no new reading; activate it again and take fresh sky to continue measuring.
ph.apertureReadout: Size {selector} · diameter {diameter} arcmin · sky area factor {factor}.
ph.apertureHelp: Three checked native sizes are available: 5, 10 and 15. Changing size clears the current or unfinished integration. Existing sky readings keep their original size and scale by aperture area for the next object reading. Prior notebook entries are retained. No aperture-loss correction is supplied.
ph.apertureOrigin: Measured at aperture size {selector}; retained as a reference-area rate.
ph.retainedTelescope: Retained photometer work belongs to {name}. Prior readings and notebook entries keep this origin. Fresh sky is required after activating an admitted telescope.
ph.telescopeProfile: Photometer profile: {name} · zero point {zero} · original seeing {seeing} arcsec.
ph.telescopeHelp: Take fresh sky after each telescope change, even on return. B and V must use the same telescope and aperture. Keep observing settings consistent when interpreting a cluster diagram; no correction for aperture losses or combining different telescopes is supplied. Prior notebook values retain their original telescope.
ph.telescopeTargetReset: The previous target is outside this telescope’s checked count domain. The default target {target} is selected for fresh sky. Existing notebook records are retained.
ph.plotPairPolicy: Each star uses its most recently confirmed B/V pair. Confirming a new pair replaces its plotted pair and invalidates previous fits; all notebook entries remain available.
ph.plotMixedSettings: These manual points mix telescopes or aperture sizes. Their captured V flux can differ: no correction for aperture losses or combining telescopes is supplied. Consider these settings before confirming a fit.
ph.plotSettings: Acquisition settings for the manual points
ph.unavailableMean: OpenVireo per-draw mean bound for this telescope profile.
ph.unavailableSeries: OpenVireo all-settings profile: a checked configuration’s expected longest total exceeds the count ceiling.
ph.unavailablePhotonDomain: Outside this telescope’s verified numerical domain.
ph.listScope: PLEIADES.HTL names the exercise list. Inclusion in that list and an exact catalog match do not establish cluster membership or spectral class. This tool does not classify stars from other fields.
ph.plotMembershipScope: These points are manual measurements from the exercise list. The diagram and your fit do not establish cluster membership or assign a spectral class.
ph.domainTitle: Why are six Mayall targets unavailable?
ph.domainMean: Each callback makes separate source and sky Poisson draws. OpenVireo limits each individual draw’s mean to 1,000,000 photons; their sum can exceed 1,000,000. This is a numerical protection of this port; the recovered original sampler and callback do not impose that threshold.
ph.domainCount: The original photometer checks actual period and cumulative totals against 2,147,483,647 before storing integer counts. OpenVireo also withholds a target when the expected longest supported series exceeds that ceiling, so one profile can retain all its listed settings. This conservative target-level rule is an OpenVireo policy.
ph.domainHint: The original overflow message suggests shorter integration time, fewer integrations or a smaller telescope. That does not validate a shorter-series route in this port. Choosing a shorter series here leaves these six targets unavailable; use an already admitted telescope profile.
ph.domainNumbers: Approximate analytic expectations, not acquired counts. Each maximum is taken over U/B/V and all three aperture sizes. The configuration shown maximizes the combined source + sky callback mean; its expected total is that sum × 5,000 callbacks (100 s × 5). The individual-draw maximum is checked separately. Actual stochastic totals can differ and remain guarded.
ph.domainTable: Six Mayall exclusions in the current OpenVireo profile
ph.domainUnchanged: The numerical kernels, target domains, readings and saved-session rules are unchanged. This explanation enables no additional acquisition.
ph.domainSummary: These are limits of OpenVireo’s verified Mayall profile, not a classification of the stars or a universal ban in the original program. Expand the evidence for the two different numerical reasons.
ph.domainSelected: These limits describe the selected Mayall profile. Existing readings always keep their recorded telescope; activate explicitly to use the selected profile for new readings.
ph.domainRetained: These limits describe the retained Mayall photometer profile. The selected Observatory telescope is shown above; existing readings keep their recorded telescope.
motion.title: Move the telescope
motion.help: Hold a direction button with the pointer, Space or Enter; release to stop. Motion updates the actual pointing and the shared observatory clock. Acquisitions are released before motion.
motion.draftHelp: For a coordinate slew, edit RA/Dec under Enter coordinates in the target card. Existing Point telescope and quarter-field browse controls remain immediate shortcuts. The programmed slew temporarily uses the original 16× setting; your manual multiplier is retained.
motion.idle: Motion stopped. No motor command has been started.
motion.moving: Telescope moving. Instrument acquisition is unavailable.
motion.complete: Programmed slew finished under the admitted axis rules. Tracking retains its previous setting.
motion.limited: Motion stopped at its last committed position by a clock or admitted motion-domain limit. No uncommitted motion interval was applied; the observatory clock was paused. Review the admitted controls before starting again.
motion.stopped: Motion stopped at the current committed pointing. The shared clock may continue; Pause observatory clock stops both.
motion.invalid: Motion was not started. Use finite RA from 0 (inclusive) to 24 (exclusive) hours and declination within ±85°. A numerical comparison too close to an unresolved boundary is withheld; existing work is retained.
motion.scope: Bounded compiled-default motion. Nominal 20 ms manual and 1 ms programmed callbacks use the recovered coordinate increments; browser timing is not a native Windows timing witness. Stop, navigation, hidden tabs, save and restore safely release motion. Moving-source photons, instructor overrides and original global event ordering remain unavailable.
motion.confirmHelp: Confirm to move from the current pointing. Cancel leaves the pointing unchanged. The current acquisition is released; no photons are generated during motion. A saved investigation restores stopped and retains your manual multiplier. A tiny initial RA difference within the recovered tolerance is retained rather than snapped.
motion.same: Target already matches the current coordinates. No slew was started.
sky.searchHelp: Search listed names or identifiers. Hubble or Hubble.HTL selects the original Hubble list. Choose a target, then Point telescope. Escape clears the filter.
sky.searchNone: No matching targets. Your current target stays available.
htl.title: Original hot lists
htl.help: Open an original CLEA HTL file, edit its targets and save a native-format list. Selecting a row does not move the telescope.
htl.separate: Hot lists are separate documents. This list is shared with the radio telescope panel’s Slew ▸ Hot List, whose Load replaces it. Save HTL before reloading; investigation JSON does not include this editor or its unsaved list.
htl.cancelled: HTL load cancelled. The confirmed list was kept.
htl.readError: The HTL file could not be read. The confirmed list was kept.
htl.error.size: The HTL file exceeds the supported 86,000-byte / 1,000-record limit. The confirmed list was kept.
htl.error.layout: Invalid HTL layout: expected a headerless sequence of 86-byte records. The confirmed list was kept.
htl.error.text: Unsupported HTL text. IDs hold up to 24 bytes and remarks up to 40. New or changed IDs must be nonblank. New text must be printable ASCII; existing imported high-byte characters may be kept unchanged while editing the ASCII around them.
htl.error.number: Unsupported HTL Extended coordinate: nonfinite, noncanonical or too small for a nonzero browser Number.
htl.error.coordinates: Enter finite coordinates with a decimal dot: RA from 0 to less than 24 hours and declination from −90 to +90 degrees.
htl.error.index: Choose an existing HTL row before editing.
htl.error.limit: The list already has 1,000 records. Remove a record before adding another.
htl.saved: HTL download prepared. Unchanged fields retain their original bytes.
htl.changed: List changed. Save HTL to keep this version.
htl.newNotice: New empty HTL list. Add a target to begin.
htl.newSource: New list · no original source file
htl.editHelp: Keep ID/remarks within their original byte capacities. New characters must be printable ASCII; existing imported high-byte characters can stay in the same order. Unchanged coordinates keep their full Extended bytes; coordinate edits use browser Number precision.
htl.pointHelp: Open the dome, then point explicitly. An existing catalog target is selected only when its ID and coordinates match exactly; otherwise its catalog selection stays unchanged. This does not enable another acquisition target.
htl.limits: The list keeps row order and repeated identifiers. New targets and coordinate edits do not add telescope acquisition support.
cursor.title: Mark a feature on the curve
cursor.help: Choose Mark center and mark your approximate line center. Then choose Mark continuum shoulder and mark one point on each side. The height you choose sets the manual continuum; no line or continuum is selected for you.
cursor.keyboard: Hold and release inside the plot to mark; releasing outside or pressing Escape cancels the preview. With the plot focused, arrow keys move the cursor (Shift moves farther), Enter or Space applies the selected tool. Numeric fields below remain available.
cursor.figure: Practice spectrum for manual wavelength and intensity marks
cursor.surface: Manual spectrum cursor: arrows move, Enter applies, Escape cancels
cursor.empty: No cursor preview. Confirmed manual inputs are kept.
cursor.policy: Cursor height is your selected trace level, not sampled source flux. Marking a center rechecks the right shoulder first and then the left against the remaining marks; valid brackets are retained, invalidated draft pairs clear. Confirmed width records stay unchanged. Calculate and review the width separately.
cursor.invalid: Mark a center strictly inside this spectrum's allowed interval first. Each shoulder must lie on a different side of that center with a positive continuum height up to 1.
cursor.shoulderHint: Move the cursor left or right of the center before applying a shoulder. The two shoulders are chosen manually.
probe.title: Read spectral intensity
probe.intro: Choose a comparison spectrum and enter a wavelength. Read each source explicitly to compare its relative intensity at the same wavelength.
probe.invalidWavelength: Enter a decimal wavelength from 3900 to 4500 Å using a dot. No scientific work was changed.
probe.invalidSource: The spectrum could not be associated with its retained source identity. No scientific work was changed.
probe.manual: Inspection only: this does not choose a continuum, record a measurement or fill your classification. The wavelength and readout are temporary; transcribe your interpretation yourself.
probe.policy: This uses the recovered endpoint-grid quadratic sampler. Intensity traces retain the printed coordinates; numerical readouts and photographic strips reconstruct the uniform grid from the retained file endpoints. Finite interpolation overshoot is not clipped or normalized by this numerical readout.
probe.scope: The recovered numerical sampler is used in 3900–4500 Å under the displayed source policy. The full photographic display, native pixel/event behavior and x87 equivalence remain unverified.
probe.unsupportedGrid: This curve remains available for visual comparison. Numerical sampling needs at least three rows and an endpoint grid within both 0.01 Å and 1% of one channel of every printed coordinate (plus 1e-9 Å numerical allowance). No curve or manual work was changed.
probe.loadedPolicy: Loaded-curve Number policy: relative intensity from the retained normalized file, using its endpoint-reconstructed grid. Every printed wavelength must agree within both 0.01 Å and 1% of one channel (plus 1e-9 Å numerical allowance). This is an added admission guard. Counts, noise, scale and continuum are not recalculated; importing a file does not grant acquired or original-practice provenance.
probe.originImported: Imported file · byte-hashed and reparsed; original authorship and acquisition origin are unverified
probe.originAcquired: Acquired stellar snapshot · replay-verified journal; normalized source-plus-sky derivative
probe.originOriginal: Original library file · verified catalog identity and byte hash
photo.help: Each photo is scaled to its own visible sampled maximum. Gray levels across sources are not a common flux scale. The numerical readout still reports the retained relative intensity.
photo.policy: Each curve samples 500 positions over the displayed wavelength window: minimum + i × (maximum − minimum) / 500, i = 0…499. The right endpoint is excluded. Each curve uses its own positive visible maximum. Reverse is applied before the recovered square-root transfer and integer/low-byte gray conversion. JavaScript Number and SVG remain declared browser adapters, not native x87/GDI equivalence.
photo.limits: Combined layout, zoom and wavelength pan use recovered static contracts. Native cursor gestures, feature tools and x87/GDI equivalence remain unverified.
photo.caption: {label} · {polarity}
photo.unavailable: Photo unavailable for this curve under the numerical source/grid policy. Its existing intensity trace is retained; original reference photos remain independently available.
photo.noPeak: Photo unavailable: this visible curve has no positive sampled maximum. Its intensity trace is retained without inventing a grayscale normalization.
photo.plotPolicy: Photographic strips use recovered endpoint-grid sampling and a separate visible-maximum display scale for each source. Gray levels are not a common physical flux scale or detector exposure. A labelled trace fallback retains its original printed coordinates.
photo.invalidSource: Photo hidden: this curve could not be associated with its verified source identity. Reload the comparison sources. No fallback trace is shown for this source-integrity failure.
photo.scrollLabel: Photographic strip and wavelength scale; scroll horizontally to inspect all columns
photo.scrollHelp: On a narrow screen, scroll horizontally or focus this image and use the arrow keys to inspect the whole wavelength interval. Available photo strips scroll together across the same displayed wavelength interval.
photo.regionNote: Manual draft wavelength markers: left {left} Å · center {center} Å · right {right} Å. The outlined continuum projects your manual heights; it does not measure brightness or calculate a width.
photo.acquiredPolicy: The acquired source-plus-sky derivative and the atlas have not been continuum-matched. Photo display scaling does not subtract sky, remove noise or provide a physical spectral type.
photo.importedPolicy: Imported bytes and printed samples are retained; photo uses its admitted endpoint-grid profile. A labelled unavailable-photo fallback keeps the original printed-coordinate trace. File names and header claims do not establish acquisition or original authorship; no continuum matching or wavelength alignment is supplied.
combined.layout: Combined view shows the upper reference photo, the unknown photo and the same unknown as a sampled intensity trace below. The lower atlas reference remains selected in the comparison pair but is not displayed here. Switch rendering to inspect it.
combined.traceUnavailable: Sampled unknown trace unavailable under the admitted source, positive-maximum or integer-height policy. The labelled printed-coordinate trace is retained.
combined.tracePolicy: The unknown uses the same 500 sampled positions and positive visible maximum as its photo. The trace has a 100-pixel amplitude with nearest-even integer heights. Reversing the photos does not reverse this trace. This is a display scale; numerical readings still report retained relative intensity.
combined.regionPolicy: Continuum marks project the selected source’s manual inputs without scaling by the displayed peak. Equivalent-width calculation remains a separate reviewed action.
combined.scrollLabel: Sampled unknown trace and wavelength scale; scroll horizontally with the other strips
viewport.help: Zoom up to 16×, pan by 10% of the current interval, or reset to the applied full wavelength range. A retained cursor marker takes priority over the diagnostic line. Only markers snapped to interior columns 1–499 center zoom; boundary/outside markers use the window center for zoom in and cached center for zoom out. Printed traces crop their existing points without resampling or peak normalization; labelled photo fallbacks retain the applied full range. The separate manual continuum tool has its own wavelength window, reset to the applied range. These display settings are not saved in investigation JSON.
combined.invalidSource: Sampled unknown trace hidden: source identity or integrity checks failed. No fallback curve is shown.
inspection.title: Comparison cursor readout
inspection.help: Mouse: press and hold inside a comparison pane, move, then release to retain the reading and wavelength marker. Photo reads sample the retained spectrum at X; trace reads report your vertical display ordinate. Arrows or keypad 2/4/6/8 preview one display column/pixel; Enter or Space retains, Escape cancels. Hover alone does nothing. The difference curve has no cursor inspection. Touch swipes scroll by default; enable touch cursor inspection above the comparison panes to hold/move/retain instead.
inspection.window: Reading taken in the {minimum}–{maximum} Å window.
inspection.error: Cursor inspection unavailable for this position or verified source.
inspection.policy: Cursor readings and markers are temporary. A trace ordinate is selected by your cursor height; it is not a sampled source flux. Printed traces use the existing 0–1 axis; the combined trace uses the recovered 100-pixel amplitude. Nothing fills a classification answer, continuum shoulder, equivalent width or saved measurement.
inspection.touchOption: Enable touch cursor inspection (otherwise swipe to scroll)
sampledTrace.caption: {label} · sampled intensity trace (visible maximum = 1)
sampledTrace.policy: Each source uses 500 endpoint-grid positions in the displayed interval and its own positive sampled maximum. The recovered trace maps intensity / visible maximum to a 100-pixel amplitude, rounded to nearest-even integer heights. Index 0 is included; the right endpoint is excluded. This is a display scale, not a shared flux or continuum calibration. Numerical source readings keep their retained relative intensities.
sampledTrace.help: Upper reference, unknown and lower reference are sampled independently. Zoom and pan resample the visible window; the original printed samples and manual work are unchanged. Reverse photographic grayscale does not reverse these traces.
sampledTrace.limits: Static native unknown/standard trace routines support this bounded Number profile; native x87/GDI equivalence, wider configuration and full difference rendering remain unverified. Entering this optional sampled view clears difference as a browser bracket-only policy.
sampledTrace.plotPolicy: Sampled traces have a separate visible-maximum display scale for each source. Equal heights across sources do not establish equal physical flux or continuum matching. Wavelength markers do not calculate continuum heights or equivalent width. A labelled fallback retains its original full printed coordinates.
sampledTrace.invalidSource: Sampled intensity trace hidden: source identity or integrity checks failed. No fallback curve is shown.
sampledTrace.unavailable: Sampled intensity trace unavailable under the admitted source, positive-maximum or integer-height policy. The labelled full printed-coordinate trace is retained.
sampledTrace.acquiredPolicy: The acquired source-plus-sky derivative and the atlas have not been continuum-matched. Trace display scaling does not subtract sky, remove noise or provide a physical spectral type.
sampledTrace.importedPolicy: Imported bytes and printed samples are retained; the sampled trace uses its admitted endpoint-grid profile. A labelled unavailable-trace fallback keeps the original printed-coordinate trace. File names and header claims do not establish acquisition or original authorship; no continuum matching or wavelength alignment is supplied.
sampledTrace.scaleNote: Visible maximum = 1 for this curve. Heights are a display scale; read retained relative flux separately.
reverseTrace.help: Turns the sampled intensity traces and the combined unknown trace upside down: each height becomes 1 minus its height, so the visible maximum lies on the bottom line. Printed traces, both difference views and the printed fallbacks never reverse. This is separate from Reverse photographic grayscale and is not saved. The web checkbox directly exposes the recovered sampled-trace inversion; native option-dialog delivery and browser pixels are not reproduced.
reverseTrace.unavailable: Reverse trace displays is available with Sampled intensity traces or Combined photo and trace, in Adjacent standards.
reverseTrace.caption: {name} · reversed
reverseTrace.readOnly: Reversed display is view-only — turn Reverse off to use the cursor or marks, or type the five values in the equivalent-width inputs.
sampledDiff.help: Compare the upper reference and unknown after scaling each by its own visible maximum. This supplemental preview uses the current wavelength window; the main comparison and manual record mode stay selected above.
sampledDiff.domain: This preview currently requires the same complete original printed grid as the existing difference display. Acquired and other imported grids remain outside this bounded profile.
sampledDiff.caption: Normalized shape difference · {standard} minus {unknown}
sampledDiff.scale: The horizontal line is zero: reference / reference visible maximum minus unknown / unknown visible maximum. This is a shape difference, not a subtraction of absolute or retained source flux.
sampledDiff.recordPolicy: The derived preview is temporary and has no cursor or width measurement. Source-flux readings and manual records remain separate.
sampledDiff.scrollLabel: Normalized sampled difference and wavelength scale; scroll horizontally or use arrow keys
sampledDiff.invalidSource: Difference preview hidden: reference or unknown source identity/integrity association failed. No fallback is shown.
sampledDiff.unavailable: Normalized difference unavailable for this window or source profile. The labelled full printed-point difference is retained below.
sampledDiff.method: Normalized difference method and display limits
sampledDiff.limits: The recovered path samples 500 positions and subtracts unrounded normalized intensities before the 100-pixel integer-height conversion. Zero is at 75 pixels in this pane. The top corresponds to +0.75 and the bottom to −0.5. Runs at the top boundary are interrupted by the native draw/move rule; lower overflow is clipped by this browser pane. These are display bounds, not missing observations or a measurement uncertainty. Native x87/GDI matching remains unverified.
range.title: Set classification wavelength range
range.help: Choose display endpoints from 3500 to 7400 Å in steps of 100 Å, at least 100 Å apart. Apply starts at 1×; zoom and pan stay within the applied range.
range.invalid: Use endpoints from 3500 to 7400 Å in steps of 100 Å, with maximum at least 100 Å above minimum. The applied range and your work are unchanged.
range.limits: A source must cover the requested sampled window. Unavailable photo or sampled views retain a labelled full-range printed-point fallback; no extrapolation or random intensity is added. Printed views show retained points only. Manual equivalent width accepts regions inside each source's own coverage within 3500–7400 Å. Range preferences are temporary and are not saved in investigation files. Default fills the draft; Apply confirms it.
range.invalidRead: Enter a decimal wavelength from {minimum} to {maximum} Å using a dot, within the actual source coverage. No scientific work was changed.
range.readScope: The recovered numerical sampler reads within the applied {minimum}–{maximum} Å range and actual source coverage. No extrapolation or random intensity is supplied. Native pixel/event and x87 equivalence remain unverified.
widthSource.intro: Choose the actual spectrum to measure, then mark a center and two continuum shoulders or enter their values. You choose the continuum; the tool does not fit it or classify the source. Comparison marks follow the selected source’s manual inputs wherever that source is displayed. Combined view repeats the unknown and does not display the lower standard.
widthSource.persistent: Original-practice unknowns retain the existing source-bound width drafts and confirmed input records in classification/full investigation JSON.
widthSource.temporary: For this source the region and result are temporary: closing the result keeps it on screen until the source, inputs or workspace change. They are not included in JSON or CSV. Existing original-practice width records are kept separately.
widthSource.domain: Allowed interval for this spectrum: {minimum}–{maximum} Å (its own coverage within 3500–7400 Å; nothing is extrapolated).
widthSource.grid: Width calculation is unavailable for this source grid. It requires at least three samples and the admitted endpoint-grid profile readable at both ends of its allowed interval. No substitute source or interpolation policy is selected.
widthSource.identity: Width calculation is unavailable because the actual source identity/integrity association is missing. No result is supplied.
widthSource.limits: Unknown, upper and lower sources use the same recovered endpoint-grid integrand. Imported/acquired sources require their existing verified source preparation and grid admission. The tool accepts regions inside each source's own coverage within 3500–7400 Å; visible-maximum plots and the broader display range do not set the continuum or rescale source flux. Native tool geometry, formatting, x87 and result-file interchange remain unverified.
cursor.mouseButtons: With Mark center selected, left mouse marks the center and right mouse marks a continuum shoulder. A center must exist first. The shoulder tool still supports the primary button, touch and keyboard. Inspect cursor leaves the browser context menu available.
cursor.windowHelp: Zoom up to 16× around your marked center when visible. Without a visible center, zoom in uses the window midpoint and zoom out uses the retained window center. Pan by 10% of the visible interval. Marks outside the window are hidden; their numeric inputs and confirmed records are retained. Reset restores the comparison's applied range (default 3900–4500 Å). This separate tool window is not saved and does not change the comparison display or the width calculation.
sharedMarks.policy: Continuum marks project your selected source’s manual inputs. Heights are not sampled flux or photographic brightness, and do not follow each curve’s peak normalization. Off-window marks are clipped without changing numeric inputs; out-of-band photo heights remain available in the numeric fields and separate manual tool.
comparisonMark.help: Choose the equivalent-width source, then enable center marking on its comparison pane. Left mouse marks a center; right mouse marks a shoulder in that same pane. The shoulder button also supports primary click, touch and keyboard. Choose Inspect comparison panes to swipe/scroll, then enable marking again. Shoulder heights are your manual continuum, not photographic brightness or sampled flux.
comparisonMark.bound: The center has a panel origin. Shoulders must be marked in that same panel, including in combined view.
comparisonMark.unbound: Mark a center in a comparison pane first. Numeric or separate-tool edits require a new comparison center; that new center starts a fresh bracket.
comparisonMark.keyboard: With comparison marking enabled, hold and release inside the selected source’s pane to apply a mark. Releasing outside or Escape cancels. Arrows preview one visible column or 0.01 manual height; Shift moves ten. Enter or Space applies the tool. Touch marks instead of scrolling only on these enabled panes. View, layout, source and tool changes cancel held input.
comparisonMark.ready: Comparison marking enabled. Mark the center first in the intended panel, then its shoulders.
comparisonMark.inactive: Comparison panes inspect intensity. Enable manual marking in Manual equivalent width to edit a region.
comparisonMark.originError: Mark a center in this panel first. Both shoulders must share its panel; the photo and trace in combined view are separate panels. No input was changed.
comparisonMark.inputError: No mark applied. Use a center strictly inside the selected source's allowed interval and shoulders on different sides with manual heights greater than 0 and at most 1. A new center in another panel starts a fresh bracket.
paneSource.option: Select width source from the center pane
paneSource.help: With center marking enabled, a committed center can select its admitted width source. Previewing or cancelling does not switch sources. In combined view, the bottom unknown trace selects the lower standard for width calculation; the trace itself remains the unknown. Check the selected width source before calculating.
panMarks.hidden: Both shoulder marks are hidden after panning because at least one shoulder is outside the window. Your numeric inputs and confirmed records are retained. Zoom, reset or mark again to redraw the region.
widthCoordinates.pan-cleared: Width calculation is paused: panning cleared both shoulder indicators. Pan back, zoom out or reset to redraw the region before calculating. Your numeric inputs and saved records were kept.
widthCoordinates.center-x-zero: Width calculation is paused: the marked center is on the zero-column boundary. Move the center inside the comparison window and verify both shoulders before calculating. Your numeric inputs and saved records were kept.
widthCoordinates.center-y-zero: Width calculation is paused: the center is on the upper sampled pane’s zero row. Move the center below the top edge and verify both shoulders before calculating. Center height does not set the continuum.
widthCoordinates.reviewChanged: The pending width review was closed because its inputs or comparison marks changed. Check the region and calculate again; saved records were kept.
combinedWidth.planned: Automatic width selection in this bottom pane will use {source}. This trace still displays the unknown spectrum. The lower standard is not drawn in combined view; its separate width graph is available below.
combinedWidth.selected: Width source: {source}. This pane still displays the unknown spectrum. The lower standard is not drawn here; review its separate width graph below. Shoulder heights remain your manual continuum, not sampled flux.
obs.title: Observation results
obs.help: Record your own spectral type and short remarks for an original practice object. This recovered results path is separate from your free-form classification response and width records.
obs.temporary: Confirmed results are saved separately in this browser when local storage is available. Export the observation notebook for a portable backup. It is not included in investigation or classification JSON/CSV and is not a native CLEA results file.
obs.unsupported: This first observation-results path supports original practices with verified object identity. Acquired and imported spectra retain their existing manual classification workflow.
obs.append: Create a separate observation on each confirmation
obs.reuse: When unchecked, Open reuses the first result for the current object. Edit buttons select a particular recorded row.
obs.recorded: Observation result confirmed for {object}. Check the browser saving status.
obs.empty: No observation results recorded in this notebook.
obs.unavailable: Unavailable in this retained practice source.
obs.metadataPolicy: No observing timestamp, position, photometry or velocity is supplied by this practice comparison. Values are not filled from a catalog or designer defaults.
obs.unrecognized: The recovered converter yields an empty type (code 0). You may record that result or edit the text. This is not a grade.
obs.conversionTitle: How the entered type is stored
obs.conversion: The recovered case-sensitive converter removes spaces and colons, encodes recognized class/subclass/luminosity and one suffix, and can ignore other text. Reopening shows its canonical label, which can omit a zero or 9.9 subclass. Review the displayed label; no type is selected from the atlas for you. Fields use printable Windows-1252 characters. The temporary record keeps the type code and exact remarks.
obs.error.encoding: Use printable Windows-1252 characters in these fields. Your entered text and prior results were kept.
obs.error.length: An entry exceeds its original byte limit. Nothing was recorded; review the text.
obs.error.unsupported-type: A punctuation-only colon entry reaches an unsafe native string path that is not supported here. Enter a type token or leave the field empty.
obs.error.source: This object is outside the supported original-practice identity path. Existing work was kept.
obs.error.stale: The source or result changed while this form was open. Reopen it before recording.
obs.error.limit: This temporary notebook holds up to 100 results. Existing results were kept.
obs.error.record: This result cannot be opened or recorded. Existing work was kept.
obs.cache.empty: No saved observation notebook in this browser yet. Only confirmed results are saved.
obs.cache.saved: Observation notebook saved in this browser. Keep an exported backup: clearing site data, private browsing or using another address may remove this copy.
obs.cache.invalid: The existing local copy could not be validated. It has been preserved and will not be overwritten automatically. Download its recovery copy before explicitly restoring a valid notebook. Current edits are in memory only.
obs.cache.unavailable: The browser could not read or save this notebook locally. Current edits are in memory only; export a backup before reloading.
obs.cache.conflict: Another browser copy changed. Automatic saving has stopped to preserve both versions. Export your current notebook, then reload or explicitly restore the version you choose.
obs.file.label: Restore observation notebook JSON (up to 128 KiB)
obs.file.reading: Reading observation notebook. No existing results have been replaced.
obs.file.invalid: The file is not a supported observation notebook. Check its format, version, source identities, ordered IDs, type codes, remarks and 128 KiB limit. Current work and the local copy were kept.
obs.file.downloadError: The browser could not start the download. Your current work was kept.
obs.file.replace: File: {file}. Confirming replaces all {current} current observation results with these {incoming} results and the saved reuse/append setting. The separate browser copy is also replaced if storage is available.
obs.file.separate: Only the separate web observation notebook is replaced. Existing investigation/classification answers, records and file formats are unchanged. Cancel keeps the current notebook.
obs.file.restored: Observation notebook restored · {count} results. Check the browser saving status and keep your exported backup.
obs.file.conflict: The local copy changed after this review opened. Nothing was replaced. Cancel, export your current work and open a fresh restore review.
obs.delete.title: Confirm observation deletion
obs.delete.warning: Remove this confirmed observation from the separate web notebook? A full recovery copy will be saved before deletion. You can undo exactly, including after reload, or export that recovery. Existing classification/width records and historical files are unchanged.
obs.delete.done: Observation deleted. A recovery copy is retained. Undo or explicitly finish the deletion before modifying this notebook again.
obs.delete.pending: One deletion has a saved recovery copy. Export it or undo to restore the exact prior notebook. Finish the deletion explicitly to discard recovery and continue editing. Normal notebook export contains current rows only; export deletion recovery separately to retain both states elsewhere.
obs.delete.already: The notebook already contains the prior records. The recovery copy was retained after an interrupted operation or cleanup. Export it or finish recovery cleanup before editing.
obs.delete.different: The recovery copy belongs to a different notebook state. No automatic merge or overwrite is allowed. Export both the current notebook and recovery, then reload or explicitly finish recovery before restoring the version you choose.
obs.delete.invalid: The separate observation recovery copy could not be validated. It is preserved and notebook changes are paused. Export the recovery text before explicitly finishing recovery.
obs.delete.undone: Deletion undone. Exact prior rows, IDs, source identities, type codes, notes, order and reuse/append setting restored.
obs.delete.cleanup: Prior notebook restored and saved. Recovery cleanup could not finish; its copy is retained. Export it or finish cleanup before editing.
obs.delete.finishWarning: Permanently discard this recovery copy and keep the current notebook as it is? Export deletion recovery first if you want to retain it. This enables notebook changes and cannot itself be undone. Existing notebook and historical files are not removed.
obs.delete.finished: Deletion recovery finished. The current notebook was kept; editing is available again.
obs.delete.failed: The operation could not be safely verified. This view was kept. A staged recovery copy may exist; export current work and recovery, then reload to check the browser state before retrying. No automatic retry or merge was performed.
obs.delete.locked: An observation recovery is pending. Undo it or explicitly finish recovery before modifying or restoring this separate notebook.
nativeResults.title: Inspect saved observation DAT
nativeResults.policy: Read candidate 144-byte CLEA observation records and their stored numeric fields. A matching layout is not proof of file origin, object identity, a valid observation or a correct student answer.
nativeResults.boundary: These files stay separate from the web notebook, its recovery, acquisition and historical session/CSV files. Explicit object/remarks/type-code corrections preserve all stored time, coordinate, photometry, redshift and velocity bytes. They never fill a student response, transfer those numbers into a model or reconstruct missing native metadata.
nativeResults.fileLabel: Inspect observation DAT (up to 144000 bytes, 1000 records)
nativeResults.reading: Reading candidate observation records. The previous inspected file is kept until reading and validation succeed.
nativeResults.loaded: Inspected candidate: {file} · {count} records. Origin and observation claims remain unverified.
nativeResults.sha: SHA-256 of the exact imported bytes:
nativeResults.empty: Empty candidate file: no records to inspect. File type cannot be authenticated from an empty or headerless file.
nativeResults.unknownCode: Outside the recovered generic type-code display
nativeResults.textPolicy: Text is displayed as Windows-1252 with control/undefined bytes escaped. The original machine code page is unknown. All bytes, including unused short-string padding, are retained unchanged.
nativeResults.zeroPolicy: The original dialog leaves numeric zero blank. Zero can therefore be an unset sentinel or an actual coordinate/value; this inspection preserves its sign and does not decide which it means.
nativeResults.numberPolicy: Values below describe the stored encoding, not measurement uncertainty or physical precision. Integer bit decoding and bounded exact decimal strings do not execute or reproduce x87 arithmetic, rounding state or exception behavior.
nativeResults.kindWarning: The display kind is outside recovered values 0/1. No photometry unit is assigned to these slots.
nativeResults.memory: The original file and any edited copy stay in memory while this view is mounted. Reload requires reimporting a file. These files are not included in investigation, classification or notebook backups. Keep the original and download any edited copy before leaving.
nativeResults.binaryOnly: Outside the bounded exact decimal display; inspect the exact binary encoding.
nativeResults.noFinite: No finite canonical value is evaluated for this encoding.
nativeResults.exactBinary: Exact binary value for canonical finite encodings
nativeResults.unit.time: Native day count. The original JD display adds date-object/runtime state; this stored Double is not labelled as raw Julian Date. No calendar/UTC conversion is inferred.
nativeResults.unit.counts: Stored photometry · mean counts per second
nativeResults.unit.unknown: Photometry unit unresolved for this display kind
nativeResults.unit.dimensionless: Stored redshift Z · dimensionless; no velocity computed
nativeResults.unit.kms: Stored velocity · km/s; no recomputation or validity grade
nativeResults.number.zero: Signed numeric zero retained; native blank-field ambiguity applies.
nativeResults.number.infinity: Stored infinity; not a physical measurement
nativeResults.number.nan: Stored NaN payload; not a finite measurement
nativeResults.number.pseudo-denormal: Pseudo-denormal Extended encoding retained without evaluation
nativeResults.number.unsupported: Unsupported Extended encoding retained without evaluation
nativeResults.error.size: File exceeds the browser inspection bound of 144000 bytes or 1000 records. The prior inspected file and notebook were kept.
nativeResults.error.layout: File has a partial 144-byte record or incompatible structure. It was not partially loaded. The prior inspected file and notebook were kept.
nativeResults.error.text: A short-string length exceeds its recovered field capacity. No record was partially loaded; the prior inspected file and notebook were kept.
nativeResults.error.owner: Original bytes are unavailable for this candidate; no reconstructed file was produced.
nativeResults.error.read: The candidate file could not be read, parsed or hashed. The prior inspected file and notebook were kept.
nativeResults.error.download: The browser could not start the unchanged-byte download. The inspected file and notebook were kept.
obs.edit.help: Use Edit observation result N for a selected-row edit with one saved Undo. It requires a saved browser copy. Open observation results retains its existing first-object reuse/append behavior and does not create edit recovery.
obs.edit.review: Confirming this selected-row edit saves its prior notebook before changing the row. Undo or explicitly finish that recovery before further notebook changes. Cancel leaves the confirmed row unchanged.
obs.edit.done: Selected observation edited and saved with one recovery copy. Undo or explicitly finish edit recovery before further notebook changes.
obs.edit.unchanged: The selected observation is unchanged. No recovery copy or additional write was needed.
obs.edit.failed: The selected-row edit could not be safely saved with recovery. The confirmed row in this view and your draft were kept. A staged copy may exist; export current work and recovery, then reload to check the browser state before retrying.
obs.edit.pending: One confirmed edit has a saved recovery copy. Undo restores the exact prior notebook; finish edit recovery explicitly to keep this edit and continue. Normal notebook export contains current rows only. Export edit recovery separately to keep the prior state elsewhere.
obs.edit.undone: Edit undone. Exact prior type code, remarks, source identities, IDs, order and reuse/append setting restored.
obs.edit.finishWarning: Permanently discard this edit recovery copy and keep the current notebook? Export edit recovery first if you want to keep the prior state. This enables notebook changes and cannot itself be undone. No current observation is removed.
obs.edit.finished: Edit recovery finished. The current notebook was kept; editing is available again.
obs.recovery.finishWarning: This recovery copy could not be validated. Export its unchanged text before discarding it. Finishing removes only that recovery copy and keeps the current notebook exactly as it is;it cannot itself be undone.
obs.recovery.finished: Observation recovery finished. The current notebook was kept;editing is available again.
program.title: Original program list
program.help: Choose a row from the original 25-entry CLASSIFY.LST or a local list of admitted practices, then advance through that sequence. These controls select practice spectra, not comparison standards. No response is filled or recorded for you.
program.unavailable: Select Original practice library first. Acquired and imported workspaces keep their separate source identities.
program.scope: Choose one of the 25 admitted original practices, or preview a local list containing only their original spectrum filenames. Cancel keeps the active list, spectrum and work.
program.draftPolicy: Before changing to another object, confirm any current manual response with Review classification and Save classification. These controls never silently discard an unrecorded response. Repeating the same object keeps its draft.
program.reading: Loading and checking the selected original practice… The current source and work stay in place until verification succeeds.
program.loaded: Program list loaded {object}. Confirmed records, notebook and recovery copies were kept.
program.cancelled: Program-list selection or load cancelled. The current spectrum and work were kept.
program.end: No More Spectra. You are at the end of the spectra list. The last object and your work are unchanged; the list does not wrap.
program.draftError: Your current manual type or reasoning is not confirmed in a matching classification record. Use Review classification and Save classification before changing objects. The current spectrum and draft were kept.
program.selectionError: This is not an admitted original program-list selection. The current spectrum and work were kept.
program.loadError: The selected practice could not be verified or its context changed. The previous source, position, draft and confirmed work were kept. Retry the selection or cancel.
program.fullDraftError: The classification log has reached 100 records. Your current manual response was kept. Save classification session or Save complete investigation to export the draft, then explicitly clear both response fields before changing objects. Review classification cannot add another record while this log is full.
obs.rowActionsHelp: Edit or delete any stored practice row while comparing an admitted library practice. The form identifies the selected observation.
programImport.input: Import program LST (ASCII, up to 64 KiB)
programImport.policy: Local lists accept two single-quoted fields per row: label and admitted spectrum basename. ASCII, space separators, CRLF/LF, up to 64 KiB and 1000 rows. Paths, other encodings and unverified spectra are rejected. Labels are display aliases; records retain the original source identity. Imported lists are temporary: reload or successful session restore returns to the original list; existing JSON/CSV does not save this configuration.
programImport.preview: Candidate list: {file} · {total} rows. It becomes active only after a selected practice is verified.
programImport.parsing: Reading and checking the candidate list…
programImport.size: The list must contain 1–1000 rows within 64 KiB. The active list and work were kept.
programImport.encoding: Unsupported list encoding or line ending. Use printable ASCII with CRLF or LF; tabs, BOM and other controls are not admitted. The active list and work were kept.
programImport.source: Row {row}: use an admitted original practice spectrum basename, without directories or URLs. The active list and work were kept.
programImport.row: Row {row}: expected exactly two nonempty single-quoted fields separated by spaces. Blank rows, comments, embedded quotes and extra fields are not admitted. The active list and work were kept.
programImport.readError: The list could not be read. The active list and work were kept.
programImport.unbound: Select a row explicitly in Program List before using Next. Another practice selection does not determine a position among repeated entries.
programImport.reset: Temporary program-list configuration reset to the original 25-entry list after session restore. Saved responses, observations and recovery were kept.
programImport.currentPreview: Current list: {file} · {total} rows. This list is already active. Choose a row explicitly to verify and load it.
nativeEdit.title: Edit owned DAT text fields
nativeEdit.record: Selected file record {index}. Other records and every stored time, coordinate, photometry, redshift and velocity byte stay unchanged.
nativeEdit.policy: Only fields you explicitly change are written. Changing an object label or manual type does not retarget coordinates or recalculate time, photometry, redshift or velocity. This is a bounded correction of supplied bytes, not the full native numeric-dialog validation or a guarantee that an original installation will accept the file.
nativeEdit.typeCurrent: Stored spectral type: {label} · int32 code {code}. Kept unless you explicitly replace it.
nativeEdit.replaceType: Replace stored spectral type code manually
nativeEdit.type: DAT manual spectral type (up to 12 bytes)
nativeEdit.encoding: Changed fields admit printable Windows-1252 only; unsupported Unicode is rejected without replacement or truncation. Spaces remain significant. Original escaped/control text, unknown type codes and unused text tails stay untouched unless you explicitly change those fields. The existing type converter is not a correctness grade.
nativeEdit.saving: Hashing the candidate edited copy… The prior file stays in place until confirmation completes.
nativeEdit.saved: DAT text/type correction confirmed in memory. Download the edited copy to keep it. The original file and all stored time, coordinate, photometry, redshift and velocity bytes remain unchanged.
nativeEdit.unchanged: No byte changes were made. The original file, edited copy and existing Undo were kept.
nativeEdit.modified: An explicitly edited copy is displayed. The unchanged source remains available separately.
nativeEdit.undone: Last DAT text edit undone exactly. Earlier confirmed edits, if any, remain in the displayed copy.
nativeEdit.revertWarning: Restore the original bytes of {file}? All confirmed edits in the current file copy will be discarded.
nativeEdit.replaceWarning: Replace the edited file with verified input {file}? The current edited copy and its Undo will be discarded.
nativeEdit.backup: Download the edited copy before replacing it if you want to retain those changes. Cancel keeps the current file and exact Undo.
nativeEdit.reverted: Original DAT bytes restored. Record selection was reset.
nativeEdit.replaced: Verified input replaced the previous file after your explicit confirmation.
nativeEdit.error.owner: This edit does not belong to an owned imported file. The current file and work were kept.
nativeEdit.error.stale: The file, row or surrounding context changed. This pending edit cannot be applied; the current file and work were kept.
nativeEdit.error.index: Select an existing record from the inspected file before editing.
nativeEdit.error.fields: Only the admitted object label, remarks and manual spectral-type fields can be changed.
nativeEdit.error.encoding: Changed fields must use printable Windows-1252 characters. Unsupported Unicode or controls were not replaced; your draft and file were kept.
nativeEdit.error.length: Use at most 15 bytes for the object label, 36 for remarks and 12 for the manual type. No field was truncated; your draft and file were kept.
nativeEdit.error.unsupportedType: A colon-only type reaches an unsafe original parsing path and is unsupported. The type and file were kept.
nativeEdit.error.input: The text correction could not be validated. Your fields and previous file were kept.
nativeEdit.error.hash: The edited copy could not be hashed. Your fields and previous file were kept; retry or cancel.
nativeEdit.preview: Replacement int32 code: {code} · {label}. Re-parsing an old displayed label can change its stored code even if the label looks the same. Leave replacement off to retain the exact original code.
nativeDelete.title: Delete owned DAT record
nativeDelete.warning: Delete file record {index}: {object}? This removes its complete 144-byte record from the edited copy.
nativeDelete.policy: The original input remains available. Other records keep their exact bytes and order. One Undo restores the immediately preceding edit or deletion; cancelling preserves it. An empty edited file contains zero records. Download your edited copy before leaving or reloading.
nativeDelete.saved: The selected record was removed from the edited copy. Original bytes remain available; one Undo restores this deletion.
nativeDelete.undone: The deleted record and its prior position were restored exactly.
nativeEdit.escapeWarning: This field contains stored non-printable bytes displayed as escapes such as \x01. Editing the displayed text writes literal characters instead of those bytes. Leave the field locked to preserve its bytes, or explicitly enable full text replacement.
nativeEdit.replaceObject: Explicitly replace escaped DAT object bytes
nativeEdit.replaceRemarks: Explicitly replace escaped DAT remarks bytes
nativeResults.dialogCancelled: DAT import cancelled because another dialog is open. Existing data and Undo were kept.
nativeList.title: Review DAT list transformation
nativeList.review: Current records: {before}. Resulting records: {after}. Confirming resets selection to the first record.
nativeList.policy: Records are inserted by stored time, then RA, retaining duplicates and all 144 bytes of each record. Equal-key placement follows the recovered insertion cursor; appending starts at the tail after a full display readout. Only canonical normal and zero time/RA keys are admitted. This is not a general x87 runtime equivalence claim. Atomic confirmation and one-level Undo are web safety measures.
nativeList.active: Native results ordering active · display-refreshed tail cursor profile
nativeList.receiptsPolicy: Names, SHA-256 and input counts are temporary session receipts, not per-record provenance. They are not stored in DAT or investigation/notebook exports. Reload or raw replacement clears this history. Up to 1000 append operations are retained; download and reimport to start a new history.
nativeList.empty: Empty DAT input: current bytes, selection and Undo are unchanged.
nativeList.saved: DAT list transformation confirmed. Selection reset to the first record. Original input remains available.
nativeList.undone: DAT list transformation undone. Previous bytes, ordering mode, receipts and selection restored.
nativeList.error.owner: DAT ordering requires privately owned input bytes and an established list.
nativeList.error.key: Cannot order this DAT: time or RA contains an encoding outside the admitted canonical normal/zero keys. Raw inspection and unchanged download remain available.
nativeList.error.limit: DAT merge exceeds the 1000-record or 1000-append browser bound. Current data and Undo are unchanged.
nativeList.error.order: The supplied revision does not preserve the established DAT ordering.
nativeList.error.format: DAT list loading accepts DAT files only. CSV/TXT loading has a separate, unported native contract. A DAT extension does not authenticate its contents.
nativeList.replaceWarning: Replace the entire current working list with this supplied DAT, ordered from an empty list? This does not append. Confirming an empty input clears the working list. Cancel keeps all current records and prior Undo; after confirmation, one Undo can restore them.
nativeText.title: Inspect native saved text results
nativeText.policy: Read supplied text claims using recovered native layouts. TXT inspection and bounded general CSV projection keep original bytes separate from DAT, the notebook, acquisitions and investigation exports. These are input claims, not verified observations or student answers.
nativeText.dateBoundary: The native “MJD(Days)” field is incomplete without its importing session: the reader prepends three characters from the native current JD and subtracts a runtime bias. No calendar date, UTC, standard MJD or native DAT time is inferred here.
nativeText.fileLabel: Inspect native results TXT (up to 512 KiB, 1000 rows)
nativeText.separator: TXT decimal separator for lexical inspection
nativeText.localeBoundary: Choose the supplied decimal separator explicitly. Exact decimal spellings are inspected without floating-point conversion. Native locale grammar, rounding and exceptional encodings are not reproduced; non-admitted spellings remain raw text.
nativeText.unresolvedDate: Original time text only. Native session prefix and bias are unresolved; no date conversion is applied.
nativeText.decimal: Exact supplied decimal spelling: {sign}{coefficient} × 10^{exponent}. No native floating-point encoding is constructed.
nativeText.invalid: Outside the admitted decimal spelling for this separator. Raw field retained; no replacement value is assigned.
nativeText.blankPolicy: Blank source field retained. No measured zero or missing value is invented.
nativeText.textClaim: Original text claim retained. No notebook response or classification grade is assigned.
nativeText.temporary: Saved-text inspection is temporary and is not included in notebook or investigation backups. Download preserves original file bytes; reloading clears this candidate.
nativeText.profile.exercise4: Recovered exercise-code-4 layout: V(Mag), Z, velocity and comments. The file does not establish the active native exercise.
nativeText.profile.counts3: Recovered three-filter counts layout with coordinates, Z, spectral type and comments.
nativeText.profile.counts5: Recovered five-filter counts layout with coordinates, Z, spectral type and comments.
nativeText.profile.magnitudes3: Recovered three-filter magnitude layout with coordinates, Z, spectral type and comments.
nativeText.profile.magnitudes5: Recovered five-filter magnitude layout with coordinates, Z, spectral type and comments.
nativeText.error.size: TXT exceeds the 512 KiB or 1000-row browser bound. Current inspection remains unchanged.
nativeText.error.encoding: This TXT reader admits ASCII plus the native degree-sign byte, with LF or CRLF. UTF-8/UTF-16 and other encodings are not admitted. Current inspection remains unchanged.
nativeText.error.header: Choose a TXT file with one of the five exact recovered result headers. Use the CSV command for its separately admitted layouts; unknown headers and other exercises remain unsupported.
nativeText.error.row: A TXT row is blank, too short or exceeds the admitted row bound. Current inspection remains unchanged.
nativeText.error.owner: The original TXT bytes are not owned by this inspection.
nativeText.error.read: Could not read or hash this saved text. Current inspection remains unchanged.
nativeText.error.dialog: TXT import cancelled because another dialog is open. Current inspection remains unchanged.
nativeText.error.csv: CSV is outside the admitted unquoted general native headers, field widths or coordinate spellings. The exercise-code-4 CSV route, quoted fields and ambiguous separators remain unsupported. Current inspection is unchanged.
nativeText.error.csvProfile: Cannot establish an admitted CSV counts/magnitude layout. First U must have one decimal digit (counts) or three (magnitudes), with consistent nonblank photometry. Header-only, blank first U or mixed precision stays unsupported. Current inspection is unchanged.
nativeCsv.fileLabel: Inspect native results CSV (up to 512 KiB, 1000 rows)
nativeCsv.separator: CSV projected-field decimal separator for lexical inspection
nativeCsv.projection: Fields below are the recovered native fixed-column projection of admitted general CSV rows. Coordinate zero-padding and spacing are projected text, not original CSV byte offsets or newly constructed native numbers. The original CSV row and download remain exact. Source CSV requires decimal points and canonical counts/magnitude precision; this separator control changes lexical inspection only.
nativeCsv.slice: Projected native column {start}, up to {width} bytes; see the original CSV row for source text.
nativeCsv.textClaim: Projected field text retained. The original CSV row remains available; no notebook response, grade or native numeric record is constructed.
nativeText.error.download: Could not download this saved-text candidate. Original input files are unchanged; reimport if byte ownership was lost after an application update.
nativeCsv.exportHashing: Preparing and hashing a separate CSV copy. Original TXT remains unchanged.
nativeCsv.exportPolicy: This copy applies the recovered native text writer to supplied canonical TXT rows. Spacing and unit delimiters change; field spellings, row order and comments must survive the checked projection. No date or native numeric record is reconstructed. The original TXT, notebook, DAT and investigation files remain unchanged.
nativeCsv.exportHashError: Could not hash this CSV copy. Original TXT and confirmed work are unchanged.
nativeCsv.exportStale: The CSV preview no longer matches the current TXT or context. Reopen the preview; no source data was changed.
nativeCsv.exportRequested: CSV browser download requested. Original TXT and confirmed work remain unchanged.
nativeText.error.exportUnsupported: CSV export requires an owned, nonempty canonical general TXT layout that the admitted CSV reader can recover. Exercise 4, ambiguous precision, blank first U, unadmitted numeric spellings, unsupported spacing/units or encoding remain unavailable; the original TXT is unchanged.
nativeText.error.exportLoss: Native CSV spacing conversion would change an object, type, field spelling, profile or comment. Export is refused; the original TXT is unchanged.
fits.title: Inspect a saved FITS image
fits.help: Open a supplied two-dimensional float32 FITS image, inspect its pixels and retain its exact original bytes. Image inspection is separate from observing and manual results.
fits.scope: This bounded reader supports one primary image, BITPIX −32, up to 1024 × 1024 pixels, with identity scaling. It does not operate the CCD or infer calibrated counts, centroids, sky coordinates, dates or object identity.
fits.file: Open float32 FITS image (up to 5 MiB)
fits.reading: Reading and hashing a candidate image. The previous image remains intact.
fits.unpadded: The final data block has no FITS padding. The complete declared array is present; original bytes are retained without repair. This alone does not prove native origin or interoperability.
fits.renderPolicy: Web display maps the stored finite range {minimum} to {maximum} onto levels 0–255; {finite} finite pixels. Constant finite images start at level 128; nonfinite pixels are magenta. Inversion and the optional palette change only the display.
fits.axes: File row 1 is shown at the top; column 1 is on the left. This is file order, not a sky-orientation or WCS solution. Click or tap a pixel; arrow keys move without wrapping, Home selects the first pixel and End the last.
fits.pixelPolicy: Decimal values describe stored binary32 data. Bits and signed zero are retained exactly. No BSCALE/BZERO transformation or unit/date/WCS claim is applied.
fits.temporary: Inspected images stay only in this tab until closed or reloaded. Download the original file to reopen it. Investigation and notebook files do not include this temporary image.
fits.error.size: Image exceeds the 5 MiB file, 1024-pixel axis or header limits. The previous image is unchanged.
fits.error.header: Unsupported or invalid FITS header: required cards, ASCII, order, uniqueness, END and block padding must be unambiguous. The previous image is unchanged.
fits.error.profile: Only a two-dimensional primary float32 image with identity scaling is supported. Integer/float64 arrays, cubes, groups, transforms and unsupported structural keywords are refused.
fits.error.data: The declared image is truncated or has unsupported extra data, extensions or padding. The previous image is unchanged.
fits.error.pixel: Enter an integer column and row within the image. The previous pixel remains selected.
fits.error.owner: Original byte ownership is unavailable. Reopen the image; no data was reconstructed.
fits.error.dialog: Another dialog opened during the read. Close it and reopen the image; the previous image is unchanged.
fits.error.read: Could not read or hash this image. The previous image is unchanged.
fits.error.download: Could not request the image download. Original bytes are unchanged; retry the download.
palette.title: CCD / IR display palette
palette.policy: The recovered shared camera palette uses a square-root grayscale curve. Here it acts on the saved-image viewer’s web levels (0–255), with browser Number arithmetic and nearest-even rounding. This is display only, not acquisition, calibration or full native image equivalence.
palette.preview: Draft grayscale palette for web levels 0 to 255
palette.invalid: Enter whole levels from 0 to 255, with black level below white level.
palette.pending: This preview has not changed the image display. Apply to use it; Cancel keeps the previous display. Stored pixel values and file bytes stay unchanged.
palette.applied: Display palette applied: black {low}, white {high}. Stored pixels are unchanged.
palette.base: Linear web display; no camera palette applied.
palette.initial: Both recovered camera display initializers set black level 64 and white level 127. An unapplied preview starts with that interval on the viewer’s web levels.
cameraInfo.title: Compiled camera defaults
cameraInfo.scope: Inspect the original CCD or IR reference setup independently of the image viewer. These settings do not configure a camera or identify an imported image.
cameraInfo.authority: Recovered compiled fallback settings, shown for reference. Instructor overrides and the camera that produced a supplied image are not established. Pixel selection, original files and investigations remain independent.
cameraPrepare.title: CCD / IR preparation reference
cameraPrepare.scope: Nominal fields use the original compiled camera dimensions and pixel sizes with the applied telescope’s focal length. A pending telescope choice does not change this reference.
cameraPrepare.limit: These are preparation references and available control positions. They do not start an exposure, apply a filter or gain, calibrate pixels, or establish a supplied image’s field or camera.
radio.title: Radio telescope control (I06 subflow)
radio.scope: Recovered from the VIREO main window: the Radio control switch, radio scope access and the radio control panel window. Inside the panel, Tracking, Slew Rate, programmed J2000.0 pointing through Set Coordinates… and press-and-hold N/S/E/W slewing with the optional horizon limit check (Limit Slewing) are recovered; beam, receiver and pulsar signal controls are not recovered and are not simulated.
radio.menu.heading: Menu commands
radio.switch.heading: Telescope control panel
radio.switch.label: Radio control switch
radio.switch.hint: Click or press Enter to toggle. Release Enter before using it again; held Enter acts once here. Other keys are ignored, as in the original key handler.
radio.switch.disabled: Disabled until radio telescope access completes.
radio.id.heading: Accessed telescope
radio.id.request: Radio telescope access requested (original caption literal not decoded in this slice).
radio.panel.heading: Radio telescope control panel window
radio.panel.gap: This window opens and closes as in the original. Of its antenna controls (TRadioLab), Tracking, Slew Rate, programmed J2000.0 pointing and press-and-hold N/S/E/W slewing (mouse, touch, Space/Enter and, partly, the original letter and numeric-keypad keys while the panel's Drive controls have focus) are offered; receivers and signals are not recovered and are not offered.
radio.timer.heading: Pending access
radio.timer.fast: Scope timer armed with a 1 ms interval; it completes automatically.
radio.timer.random: The original waits a pseudo-random interval below {range} ms here. That interval is not reproduced.
radio.timer.domeWait: Dome state 3: the timer tick is ignored until the dome state changes.
radio.env.heading: Scenario inputs (not recovered defaults)
radio.env.help: These values come from parts of VIREO outside this slice. Supply them explicitly; nothing is assumed.
radio.env.option: Access option byte set (immediate access; dialog control unresolved)
radio.env.otherWindows: Another Window menu item is visible
radio.env.diameter: Dish diameter (whole metres, original integer field)
radio.env.diameterHelp: Shown as “<value> Meter Radio Telescope”. The recovered compiled default is 100, used when no options file loads; the value in a current classroom configuration is not known, so supply it explicitly.
radio.env.invalid: Enter a whole number from -2147483648 to 2147483647.
radio.state.heading: Recovered control state
radio.outcome.exercise-entered: Radio pulsar exercise entered: radio switch shown, optical switch hidden.
radio.outcome.exercise-required: Enter the radio pulsar exercise first; the radio access command is not reachable yet.
radio.outcome.already-accessed: The radio telescope is already accessed; the command does nothing.
radio.outcome.access-rerequested: Access requested again; the scope timer was re-armed.
radio.outcome.timer-waiting-dome: Timer tick ignored while the dome state byte is 3.
radio.outcome.accessed-by-timer: Scope timer completed: radio telescope accessed.
radio.outcome.switch-unavailable: The radio switch is disabled or hidden; nothing changed.
radio.outcome.key-ignored: Only Enter toggles the switch; nothing changed.
radio.outcome.switched-on: Radio switch on: control panel window shown.
radio.outcome.switched-off: Radio switch off: control panel window hidden.
radio.outcome.panel-reopened: Radio control panel window shown again.
radio.outcome.menu-item-hidden: The radio panel menu item is hidden; turn the radio switch on.
radio.outcome.panel-closed: Radio control panel window closed: the radio switch turned off and the window was hidden. The telescope state is kept and a running slew continues; switch on to reopen it.
radio.outcome.panel-not-shown: The radio control panel window is not shown.
radio.outcome.diameter-required: Supply the dish diameter first; the original forms the telescope caption from it. Nothing changed.
radio.error.environment: The scenario inputs are invalid; nothing changed.
obsHr.title: HR diagram from your observation results
obsHr.intro: This follows the original VIREO route File › Load/Plot › Data from Observations. Load observation results you saved earlier, plot them on the original fixed axes, then compare the zero-age main sequence and isochrones by eye. Nothing is fitted, filled in or graded for you.
obsHr.fileHelp: Original 144-byte observation records, up to 1000 records. Choosing a file does not change your current results until you add or replace.
obsHr.reviewHeading: Review the file before using it
obsHr.sources: Files used in this browser session
obsHr.downloadNote: The download contains the current records exactly as 144-byte original-format records, in the native order. It is a copy for reloading here or in other tools; it is not a new file format.
obsHr.errors.size: The file is larger than 1000 records (144000 bytes). Current results are unchanged.
