radioRoute.title: Radio telescope control
radioRoute.scope: Recovered VIREO radio telescope controls: telescope access and the control panel (Tracking, Slew Rate, slews through Set Coordinates…, and the panel clock for a radio UT you supply), Pulsar Parameters, and a main receiver with up to two channels that draws a modelled signal from the pulsar catalog. Record captures that signal for Pulsar Analysis, Identify names the capture and Align stacks the windows. A capture is model output, not an observation, and the original receiver sound is not played. Press Start pulsar exercise to set up, and open Pulsar guide for the steps.
radioRoute.scenario.heading: Chosen web scenario
radioRoute.scenario.options: Telescope options: the recovered compiled defaults, which the original uses when no options file loads (not a transit telescope, Limit Slewing off, horizon limit 10°, maximum rate index {max}, rate base {base}, instant slew off). An instructor options file can change every value; none is read here, and the current classroom configuration is not known. The radio options scenario in the panel lets you turn the recovered Limit Slewing option on or off with Apply; every other option, including the horizon limit, stays at its compiled default. Save investigation keeps the applied options; no options file is written.
radioRoute.scenario.environment: Main-window inputs start unsupplied, with the dome state byte at its initial value 0, and are not linked to the observatory dome. Choose “Use compiled defaults” (diameter 100, access option off) or enter values under Scenario inputs.
radioRoute.scenario.access: Telescope access: with the access option off the original waits a pseudo-random interval below {range} ms. That interval and its random source are not reproduced; deliver the access timer tick yourself.
radioRoute.scenario.slew: Programmed slews: slew-timer ticks arrive on a nominal {interval} ms browser interval, which is not Windows timer timing. Ticks continue while you use another tool or close the panel window. During Save or Restore investigation they pause, and missed ticks are not caught up.
radioRoute.scenario.clock: Radio clock: no time is taken from this computer or from the observatory clock. You supply a UT and choose the compiled radio longitude explicitly. Clock ticks then arrive on a nominal {interval} ms browser interval (the compiled timer default; not Windows timer timing), or one at a time with the manual tick. They continue while a radio dialog or message is open, while you use another tool and while the panel window is closed. During Save or Restore investigation scenario time stops and is not caught up.
radioRoute.scenario.gates: Not available: the rest of the original options dialog and options file, the original date dialog once the panel has been shown, the local date/time labels, the original F4/F8 keys, the original receiver sound and volume, and the hot list’s Add Current Item and Save from this panel (disabled; their enabling code is not recovered). Available: receiver Record with Identify and Properties, and Align of the receiver windows. Programmed slews to coordinates entered in J2000.0, or in B1950.0 converted with the original fixed-epoch precession, and press-and-hold N/S/E/W slews run, also with the original letter and numeric-keypad keys while Tracking or a direction button has focus; holds are cancelled when the window loses focus, the page is hidden or another operation starts. With Limit Slewing on, the horizon limit check needs a supplied radio UT: without one a slew request is refused and manual slewing waits for a clock tick, and positions too close to the limit, the zenith or the nadir for this browser version to decide are refused rather than guessed.
radioRoute.persistence: This radio telescope state is kept while this browser tab stays open, also while you use other tools; reloading the page resets it. Save investigation includes the setup, pointing, options, the radio clock (restored paused), the catalog and the receiver settings; open dialogs, slews, receiver runs and the Pulsar Parameters window are not included. Save investigation downloads a file; the download is not confirmation that it was written.
radioRoute.clock.heading: Radio clock scenario
radioRoute.clock.help: The original panel clock reads this computer’s local time plus an offset set in its date dialog; neither is used here. Enter a UT from {min} to {max} (whole seconds when entered), apply it, apply the compiled radio longitude, then use Start or the manual tick in the control panel. Save investigation keeps the applied UT, longitude and elapsed scenario time; a restored clock is paused until you press Start.
radioRoute.clock.utHelp: Gregorian date and time in UT, for example 2000-01-01T12:00:00. Enter applies it. Applying a UT pauses the clock and restarts scenario time from it.
radioRoute.clock.longitudeValue: {radians} rad, east positive (the recovered compiled radio option; an options file can change it, and no site name is implied)
radioRoute.clock.state.unsupplied: No radio UT applied: no clock tick runs, so Right Ascension does not drift.
radioRoute.clock.state.needsLongitude: UT applied; choose the compiled radio longitude before the clock can tick.
radioRoute.clock.state.domain: Stopped: scenario time passed {max}, the end of the supported range. The telescope keeps its last accepted tick. Apply a UT to continue.
radioRoute.clock.state.frozen: Running, frozen while the project operation runs.
radioRoute.clock.state.running: Running: scenario time advances with browser time. The control panel shows the last accepted tick.
radioRoute.clock.outcome.utc-applied: UT applied; the radio clock is paused at it.
radioRoute.clock.outcome.utc-invalid: That UT is not a valid YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS date and time from 1900 to 2099. Nothing changed.
radioRoute.clock.outcome.draft-cancelled: UT edit cancelled; the field shows the applied UT again.
radioRoute.clock.outcome.longitude-uncha: The compiled radio longitude is already applied.
radioRoute.clock.outcome.start-needs-utc: Apply a UT first; no default time is used.
radioRoute.clock.outcome.start-needs-lon: Apply the compiled radio longitude first.
radioRoute.clock.outcome.start-domain: The scenario time is past {max}, the end of the supported range. Apply a UT first.
radioRoute.clock.outcome.already-running: The radio clock is already running.
radioRoute.clock.outcome.not-running: The radio clock is not running.
radioRoute.clock.outcome.domain-stopped: Radio clock stopped: scenario time passed {max}, the end of the supported range. No later reading was invented; the telescope keeps its last accepted tick.
radioRoute.clock.limits: Browser limits: Julian date is formed from the UT in double precision, and sidereal time uses the existing port of the original routine. The original extended-precision arithmetic is not reproduced and no error bound against it is claimed. The observatory clock is not linked, although in the original both panels share one date.
radioRoute.clock.outcome.utc-dialog-appl: UT applied from Set Date/Time, ID; the radio clock keeps running or stays paused as before.

There it is enabled by Run after a star-catalog path check; this browser version has no Run step and offers it from exercise entry, using its bundled resources instead (a declared adaptation; Run is not claimed to have executed). The dialog is filled from the radio UT you applied. OK sets the radio clock UT, keeps it running or paused, and changes nothing on the antenna.

radioRoute.date.error.time.large: The time “{text}” is outside this browser subset: each part must be at most {max} in size.

pulsarParameters.heading: Pulsar Parameters (reference utility)
pulsarParameters.intro: The original radio exercise’s Pulsar Parameters window: browse a pulsar catalog record by record, find a pulsar by name, and compute its period at a date and a distance from its dispersion measure for an electron density you choose. The values are catalog references, not observations: nothing is received, recorded or measured here, and nothing is copied into a measurement or notebook.
pulsarParameters.persistence: The loaded catalog is kept while this tab stays open, and Save investigation keeps it: the recorded original by its identity (fetched and checked again on restore), a catalog you supplied as its values. The window and your Date and Electron Density edits are not saved, and reloading the page empties them.
pulsarParameters.reference.heading: Reference catalog
pulsarParameters.reference.help: The original reads its catalog file itself. This browser version includes the recorded VIREO Pulsars.dat, checked by size and SHA-256 before it is used: Start pulsar exercise loads it when no catalog is loaded, or choose Load bundled Pulsars.dat. You can instead choose a catalog text file in the original fixed-column layout (at most {max} bytes). Either is read into this tab’s memory only: nothing is uploaded or saved.

pulsarParameters.window.epochNote: Date (MJD) and PEpoch subtract 2,400,000 from the Julian Date, as the original does. That is the textbook MJD plus half a day; it is kept, not corrected. Numbers use binary64 arithmetic in the original’s order of operations, not its x87 precision.
pulsarParameters.window.shared.name: At Open, the receivers’ shared source name was {name}: the window opened at the first record whose J2000 name contains it, or at the first record if none does. Open did not change that name.

pulsarParameters.help.title: OpenVireo help (written for this browser version; not the original Help file)
pulsarParameters.help.body: Prev and Next step through the catalog in file order and stop at either end. Find Pulsar… searches the B1950 or J2000 names for the text you type: the first record whose name contains it (case-sensitive, first 12 characters) is shown; otherwise the record stays and a message explains. Type a Date (MJD) or an Electron Density (electrons/cm³), then choose Update or press Enter: Period is P + PDot × (Date − PEpoch) in seconds, and Distance is the dispersion measure divided by the density, rounded to whole parsecs. Exit closes the window and forgets the Find text.
pulsarParameters.help.note: These are catalog reference values for exploring the exercise. They are not measurements and are never copied into your results.
pulsarParameters.find.bounds: Up to {max} characters; the first {searched} are searched, exactly as typed.
pulsarParameters.find.tooLong: Longer than {max} characters: the edit was refused.

pulsarParameters.notice.update.note: OpenVireo wording: the original reports a conversion error with runtime-library text that is not reproduced.

radioReceiver.setup.heading: Receiver monitor
radioReceiver.note.display: A modelled display of the recovered receiver signal chain for the catalog you loaded. It is not an observation and not a recorded measurement.
radioReceiver.note.temporary: Receiver windows, receiving runs and traces are not part of Save investigation. It keeps the receiver seed, options and window settings, and Restore investigation brings them back with the receivers closed. Reloading the page without Restore resets them.
radioReceiver.note.silent: The original receiver sound is not reproduced. A separate web audition can play a stopped trace on request; it is a sonification of the stored trace, not the original sound.
radioReceiver.note.unavailable: Not available: the original Save dialog (recorded data is saved only through the web Save with verification, offered by the Record question about unsaved data and in Pulsar Analysis), the original sound and volume, dragging receiver windows, and minimizing or maximizing them.
radioReceiver.setup.seedHelp: Whole number from 0 to 4294967295. Each reseed this monitor models (receiver window creation and the first profile allocation) takes this value plus the number of earlier modelled reseeds in this session; the original seed came from the system timer.
radioReceiver.setup.seedLocked: Locked while a receiver window is open.
radioReceiver.setup.seedInvalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to 4294967295 to open a receiver.
radioReceiver.card.child: Channel window {n}: follows the main receiver's Mode and horizontal scale.
radioReceiver.align.on: Align is on: the channel windows stay stacked directly below the main receiver window, and moving a window returns it to the stack, as in the original. It arranges windows only, never signals.
radioReceiver.align.off: Align is off: the windows stay where they are; Move up and Move down rearrange them. Turning Align on stacks them again.
radioReceiver.align.staleOn: Align is on again: creating the channel window turned it on, as the original window creation does. The Align indicator still shows No until the main window's next parameter refresh (for example a Vert. Gain step). Whether the original's own window activation refreshes it sooner is not established.
radioReceiver.card.finishing: Sweep position {position} of {width}: finishing the sweep; Mode is unavailable until it ends.
radioReceiver.card.sourceNone: Profile source: not built yet (Mode builds it).
radioReceiver.canvas.label: Receiver {n} display, mode {mode}. A modelled trace; no values are listed.
radioReceiver.status.addNothing: Both channel windows are open: nothing was added, as in the original.
radioReceiver.status.stopRequested: Stop requested: the sweep finishes at the right edge.
radioReceiver.status.atLimit: {control} is at its limit (the original beeps).
radioReceiver.status.web.seed-invalid: Refused: the receiver random seed is not valid.
radioReceiver.status.web.seed-locked: The seed cannot change while a receiver window is open.
radioReceiver.status.web.no-catalog: Refused: load a reference pulsar catalog first.
radioReceiver.status.web.mark-lease-held: Another mark drag is in progress.
radioReceiver.status.web.mark-input: This mark input is not supported.
radioReceiver.status.web.mark-position-i: Enter a whole column from 0 to 400. The marks are unchanged.
radioReceiver.status.web.mark-unset: Place this mark first: type a column and press Enter, or press Home or End.
radioReceiver.status.web.mark-bound: The mark is already at the edge of the display.
radioReceiver.marks.scope: Marks read times on this modelled display: column × this window's stored sweep seconds ÷ 400. A new window starts at 4 seconds; Receive updates its snapshot. The current Horz setting may differ. Marks are not measurements, no catalog value is read, and they are not saved.
radioReceiver.marks.display: Receiver {n} display with manual marks. Press and drag on it to place a mark.
radioReceiver.marks.selectLabel: Mark placed by the primary mouse button, touch, pen and the keyboard
radioReceiver.marks.help: Mouse: the left button drags the selected mark and the right button drags the second mark. Touch or pen: drag the selected mark. Keyboard: type a column and press Enter or Place; Home and End place it at 0 and 400; Arrow Up and Arrow Down move a placed mark by one column; a step onto the other mark's column does not move it, so type a column to move past it. Escape on the display ends a drag and keeps the last position. A second mark is attempted in every window; a window whose first mark is already at that column keeps its stored second mark.
radioReceiver.marks.timerHelp: Marks are available after the sweep finishes.
radioReceiver.marks.clearHelp: Clear mark: if this window has a second mark, the second mark of every window is cleared; otherwise this window's first mark. Double-clicking the display does the same (a browser binding).
radioReceiver.marks.status.gated: Marks are available after the sweep finishes.
radioReceiver.marks.status.ended: Mark drag ended; the last accepted position is kept.
radioReceiver.marks.status.placedAll: {mark} mark set to column {x} in windows {windows}.
radioReceiver.marks.status.collision: {mark} mark not moved in windows {windows}: column {x} is the other mark's column there. The label shows the requested time.
radioReceiver.marks.status.placedSome: {mark} mark set to column {x} in windows {stored}; not moved in windows {collided}, where column {x} is the other mark's column. Their labels show the requested time.
radioReceiver.marks.status.timer: {mark} mark not moved while the sweep runs; the label shows the requested time.
radioReceiver.marks.status.clearNone: No mark to clear in this window.
radioReceiver.tickError: The receiver timer is refused: {reason} The original outcome in this case is not established. Stop is accepted but stays pending while this error persists; closing the main receiver window recovers.
radioReceiver.box.note: Original message (MessageBox information, OK). Enter or Escape closes it.
radioReceiver.box.closeOrder: Web note: the original refuses by window number, not by card position. Close Receiver {n} first, wherever its card is in the column, or close the main receiver window to close all.

radioAccess.menu.command: File ▸ Pulsar List... appears here only while the item is shown and works only while it is enabled. It selects a catalog source for the current antenna pointing with the recovered search: only the first run of records in file order near the pointing's right ascension, a limit of 2.0 on the recovered separation and the earlier record on a tie, with no wrap at 0/24 h. It is not a nearest-record search and can miss a nearer record later in the file. A selected record replaces the receivers' shared source; without one, only the shared source name is cleared. Pulsar Parameters then opens at the first record whose J2000 name contains the shared name (or at the first record), which can be an earlier record than the selected one. No receiver is opened, redrawn or reseeded at the click; open receivers may follow the new source at their next update. Exit and Find Cancel do not undo it. Save investigation keeps this item's state and the receivers' shared source, and Restore investigation brings them back without reopening Pulsar Parameters or any receiver; the download is not confirmation that a file was written.

radioRoute.exercise.heading: Pulsar exercise
radioRoute.exercise.intro: Start pulsar exercise does the setup steps for you: Radio Astronomy of Pulsars, the compiled inputs, telescope access, the Radio switch, the control panel and Tracking, a radio UT and the compiled radio longitude, then it loads the bundled pulsar catalog. Steps you already did are kept; nothing you set is reset.

pulsarLab.title: Pulsar timing guide
pulsarLab.intro: Measure a pulsar’s period and the delay between two radio frequencies by hand, and compare them with the catalog’s period and dispersion measure. The check marks follow what is in the app right now: they say a reading was recorded, not that it is correct.

pulsarLab.progressMeaning: What do the pulsar check marks mean?
pulsarLab.progressHelp: Each mark is computed from the current state: the Radio setup, the loaded catalog, the receiver windows, the capture in memory and the confirmed measurement rows of the recording shown in Pulsar Analysis. Clearing data or rows removes the marks. Closing receivers removes the pointing and channel marks but does not send you back while a capture is shown. A period or delay mark means you recorded rows with a reference and a vertical cursor (for the delay: the same reference at two or more frequencies); the guide does not check that you chose the right pulses.

pulsarLab.step.setup.title: Set up the radio telescope
pulsarLab.step.setup.help: On the Radio telescope page press Start pulsar exercise. It runs the same controls you could press yourself and applies the radio UT {ut} only if you have not applied one. Set Date/Time is available only before the control panel is activated.
pulsarLab.step.catalog.title: Load the pulsar catalog
pulsarLab.step.catalog.help: Start loads the bundled {file} when no catalog is loaded. Pulsar Parameters shows whether the loaded catalog is the recorded original file or one you supplied. If loading fails, retry, or choose a catalog file there.
pulsarLab.step.point.title: Point at a pulsar
pulsarLab.step.point.help: For a first run, open Pulsar Parameters, use Find Pulsar…, choose J2000 and enter 0332+5434 (legacy name 0329+54). Note P, DM, RA and Dec, then Exit. In Slew ▸ Set Coordinates… enter those J2000.0 coordinates, answer Yes and wait for arrival. Press Receiver and check its heading names the pulsar. Use 400 and 500 MHz for this first comparison.
pulsarLab.step.channels.title: Add channels and choose frequencies
pulsarLab.step.channels.help: Press Add for a channel window, then give the receivers at least two different frequencies with Freq., for example 400 and 500 MHz. A larger frequency difference gives a larger delay.
pulsarLab.step.channels.disarm: Add every channel BEFORE pressing Record: adding a channel disarms Record.
pulsarLab.step.channels.factor: If the pulses are cut off at the top of a display, lower that window’s display factor (Vert. gain). It changes the display only, not the recorded values.
pulsarLab.step.capture.title: Capture the signal
pulsarLab.step.capture.help: Press Record, then Mode to receive. After a few seconds press Mode again; the sweep finishes. Accept the name in Identify, read Properties, then answer No to open Pulsar Analysis. The capture is the receiver model’s output, not an observation.
pulsarLab.step.period.title: Measure the period
pulsarLab.step.period.help: In Pulsar Analysis place the reference cursor (right button) on one pulse and the vertical cursor (left button) on the same panel N pulses later. Choose Record to keep the reading.
pulsarLab.step.period.formula: Period by hand: P = (V − R) / N, in seconds, where R and V are the two cursor times and N the number of periods between them. Compare it with the catalog period in Pulsar Parameters (Period at the capture date). More periods between the cursors give a smaller reading error, about one sample interval divided by N.
pulsarLab.step.delay.title: Measure the dispersion delay
pulsarLab.step.delay.help: Keep the reference cursor. In each frequency’s panel put the vertical cursor on the same pulse and choose Record. The delay is the difference of the vertical times: the lower frequency arrives later. Compare it with the delay the catalog’s dispersion measure DM predicts.
pulsarLab.step.delay.formula: delay [s] = 4150 × DM × (1/f_low² − 1/f_high²), with f in MHz and DM in pc/cm³
pulsarLab.step.delay.source: This is the dispersion relation of the receiver model in this version (the constant 4150 recovered from the original program, src/core/radioPulsarProfile.ts). It checks your reading against the model that made the capture, not against a sky observation. The guide does not decide whether your cursors mark the same pulse.
pulsarLab.step.investigation.title: Save the investigation
pulsarLab.step.investigation.help: Press Save investigation in the toolbar. The file holds the Radio setup, pointing and paused clock, the catalog identity, the capture (or loaded .PLR) and every confirmed row with its cursors. Restore investigation in a new tab brings them back.
pulsarLab.step.investigation.note: The mark covers the capture and rows at that moment: a new capture, a load, Clear or a row or comment change needs a new Save. A browser download is not confirmation that the file was written.
pulsarLab.step.save.title: Optional: keep separate copies
pulsarLab.step.save.help: In Pulsar Analysis use Save for a verified .PLR copy of the capture, and export your measurement rows as CSV.
pulsarLab.step.save.optional: Optional, not counted: Save investigation already keeps the capture and rows.
pulsarLab.data.heading: Three kinds of data
pulsarLab.data.reference.help: Values from the pulsar catalog. They are what you compare against; they are never your measurements.
pulsarLab.data.model.help: What the receiver simulation produced from the catalog for your pointing, time and frequencies. It is not an observation of the sky.
pulsarLab.data.supplied.help: Any catalog or recording you load yourself that is not the recorded original file. Results are only as good as that file.

pulsarLab.recover.clock: Apply a radio UT and the compiled radio longitude in the Radio clock scenario card, or press Start pulsar exercise.

pulsarLab.recover.disarm: Adding a channel disarms Record. Add all channels first, then press Record again.

pulsarLab.recover.clip: Lower that window’s display factor (Vert. gain). The display does not change the recorded values.

pulsarLab.recover.catalog: Use Retry bundled catalog, or choose a catalog file under Pulsar Parameters. A file that does not match the recorded original is marked as supplied.

pulsarLab.recover.tracking: Tracking is off. Start does not switch it on for a control panel that is already on (you switched the Radio switch on yourself, or turned Tracking off). Press Tracking in the control panel.
pulsarLab.sourceHelp: Pulsars.dat is the original VIREO catalog file, included byte for byte from CLEA_Vireo.zip under the CLEA license terms recorded by the project (free non-commercial copies for students; no distribution for profit). Credit: Project CLEA, Gettysburg College, with support from NSF and Gettysburg College. It was probably derived from the ATNF Pulsar Catalogue (Manchester et al. 2005); that origin is uncertain. It is not labelled public domain or open license.
pulsarLab.limits: The receiver signal, noise and timing are this version’s port of the recovered model; no equivalence with the original program at run time is claimed. The scenario UT is a web choice.

pleiadesLab.title: Your Pleiades photometry
pleiadesLab.intro: Load the original exercise list, point the telescope at a listed star, measure its B and V magnitudes against fresh sky, transcribe your readings, form B−V and fit the cluster distance by eye. This guide follows your work; it supplies no magnitudes, colors or distance.
pleiadesLab.adaptation: Adaptation: the guide, pointing card, exercise-list button and pointing check are OpenVireo web orchestration, not recovered native instructions.
pleiadesLab.coverage: Admitted stars with your own confirmed B−V: {count} of {total}
pleiadesLab.progressHelp: Marks are recomputed from your current list, pointing and photometer work; nothing is stored. After a reload the list and pointing marks start again, while Restore investigation brings back readings, notebook entries, colors and a confirmed fit. Done means you acquired, transcribed or confirmed something, never that a value is correct.
pleiadesLab.e05: Next exercise (E05): plot your confirmed B/V pairs in Data from Observations and fit a model by eye. That view is a link here, not a counted step; finishing this guide does not complete E05.
pleiadesLab.next.list: Next: in the observatory open Original hot lists and choose Load exercise list (PLEIADES.HTL).
pleiadesLab.next.point: Next: open the dome, select an admitted row and choose Point to HTL selection.
pleiadesLab.next.activate: Next: choose Measure with photometer, then Activate Pleiades photometer.
pleiadesLab.next.measure: Next: take fresh sky through V and B, then read the star through V and B.
pleiadesLab.next.record: Next: add notebook entries with your own transcribed B and V magnitudes.
pleiadesLab.next.color: Next: choose your saved B and V readings and Calculate B−V.
pleiadesLab.next.sample: Next: change Photometry target to the next admitted star and repeat the B and V readings, transcriptions and B−V. All 16 need the 0.4m telescope; KPNO 0.9m (14) and Mayall (10) cannot finish them, and changing telescope requires fresh V and B sky in the new context.
pleiadesLab.next.distance: Next: in Exercise color–magnitude analysis enter your vertical shift m−M and confirm the manual cluster fit.
pleiadesLab.next.save: All counted steps are done. Save investigation, reload, and Restore investigation JSON to check your backup.

pleiadesLab.status.save: Instruction only: a download is not confirmation that the file was written, so this step is not counted.
pleiadesLab.step.list.title: Load the exercise list
pleiadesLab.step.list.help: Open Original hot lists in the observatory and choose Load exercise list (PLEIADES.HTL). It holds 24 original positions; 16 are admitted for photometry and 8 remain unavailable with their reason. Hot lists are not part of the investigation backup.
pleiadesLab.step.point.title: Point at a listed star
pleiadesLab.step.point.help: Open the dome, select an admitted row and choose Point to HTL selection. The Pleiades photometry card appears only when the pointing equals that row exactly.
pleiadesLab.step.activate.title: Activate the photometer on that star
pleiadesLab.step.activate.help: Choose Measure with photometer, then Activate Pleiades photometer. Check that Photometry target names the star you pointed at and that Actual telescope pointing shows its coordinates with Telescope ready. Unavailable rows and stars outside the selected telescope’s domain stay blocked.
pleiadesLab.step.measure.title: Measure sky and star through B and V
pleiadesLab.step.measure.help: Choose Sky position and take a reading through V, then through B. Choose the target position and read the star through V and B. Each target reading subtracts the same-filter sky of this activation.
pleiadesLab.step.record.title: Transcribe your readings
pleiadesLab.step.record.help: After each completed target reading choose Add notebook entry and type the magnitude you read. The field starts blank; nothing is copied from a catalog.
pleiadesLab.step.color.title: Form B−V
pleiadesLab.step.color.help: Choose your saved B and V readings of the same star and Calculate B−V. Your transcribed difference uses your own entries.
pleiadesLab.step.sample.title: Build the sample
pleiadesLab.step.sample.help: Change Photometry target inside the photometer to move to the next admitted star; the telescope follows and the filter skies of this activation remain valid. Repeat until all 16 admitted original stars have their own confirmed B−V. This is the coverage of this web exercise, not a historical classroom minimum or a grade. All 16 are measurable only with the 0.4m telescope; with KPNO 0.9m (14 stars) or Mayall (10 stars) selected you cannot finish all 16, and changing telescope requires fresh V and B sky in the new context.
pleiadesLab.step.sample.minimum: The fit itself accepts two or more confirmed pairs; a two-star trial is possible but is not the full sample.
pleiadesLab.step.distance.title: Fit the distance by eye
pleiadesLab.step.distance.help: In Exercise color–magnitude analysis move the standard sequence vertically by entering m−M, compare it with your points and confirm the manual cluster fit. A new B−V afterwards clears the confirmation.
pleiadesLab.step.distance.formula: Distance D = 10 × 10^((m − M)/5) pc, with 1 pc = 3.26 ly as in the manual; compare with the manual’s historical 410 ly reference.
pleiadesLab.step.distance.optional: The model-fit section below it is optional and is not counted here.
pleiadesLab.step.save.title: Keep your investigation
pleiadesLab.step.save.help: Use Save investigation, reload the page and Restore investigation JSON. Restored readings, notebook entries, colors and fit return; activate again before new readings.
pleiadesLab.problem.card: The Pleiades photometry card does not appear
pleiadesLab.recover.card: The card appears only when the telescope equals a listed star exactly. Point to HTL selection again; drift, browsing, motion or an edited row no longer match.
pleiadesLab.recover.blocked: Eight list positions are unavailable, and some stars are outside the checked domain of the 0.9 m or Mayall telescope. Point at another admitted row or use the 0.4 m telescope.
pleiadesLab.recover.start: Read Actual telescope pointing. Leaving the photometer, hiding the tab, changing telescope or saving releases the context; activate again. A target reading also needs fresh same-filter sky.
pleiadesLab.problem.sky: Target readings ask for sky again
pleiadesLab.recover.sky: Every activation starts a new context. Change targets inside the photometer instead of reactivating for each star, so your filter skies stay valid.
pleiadesLab.recover.budget: A photometer session holds a bounded number of events. Reactivating for every star uses it faster; save your work before starting a new seeded session.
pleiadesLab.sourceHelp: The exercise list is the unchanged original file, checked before parsing. It supplies identities and coordinates only; photometer fields, calibration and noise are the existing verified bench.

ownResults.title: Observational Results · your confirmed redshifts
ownResults.scope: Web view of your saved measurement log only; unsaved adjustments and cancelled records are never listed. Object is the label you entered on each row, including acquired rows; the source, acquisition link, target, file and SHA-256 are shown separately. Velocity is derived as v = c z from each recorded float32 z, not entered by you; it is not relativistic and not a distance. Imported file names and hashes remain your claims. This is not a native CLEA results file.

An acquisition row is linked only when its kind, SHA-256 and file name, and for galaxy acquisitions its target, match an archived acquisition. Downloads contain no timestamps; −0 is written as -0 with its bits.

Download results text or CSV, or Print results; the browser handles saving and printing. Keep the JSON session as your backup.

lss.adaptation.field: Field names come from the original list file names; the original field list file is not included.
lss.adaptation.telescope: You choose among the three verified telescopes; the original survey mode's telescope setup is not recovered.
lss.adaptation.fresh: Each pointing builds a fresh field centred on the list coordinates; the original field cache is not reproduced.
lss.adaptation.raster: Galaxy images use a declared nearest-centre browser raster, not Windows pixel identity.
lss.adaptation.range: The spectrometer range is fixed at 4000–5000 Å and every galaxy uses the original template spectrum.
lss.adaptation.measure: Measurement uses this dedicated panel with the analyser's recovered shift control.
lss.adaptation.wedge: Your records go to the wedge directly with their exact values, not through the original text file.
lss.adaptation.csv: Results are saved in an OpenVireo CSV format, not the original LSS text format.
lss.adaptation.packs: Stars come from bounded GSC read witnesses for these fields only; arithmetic uses browser numbers, not the original x87 unit.
